features.name: Bookings
features.summary: Core booking record: reserve tours/hotels/yachts for passengers with extras, supplements, itinerary, files and financial lines.

workflows.fact: A booking reserves a tour, hotel room, or yacht for one or more passengers, one of whom must be marked as the booking client (the primary contact) — exactly one, never zero or more than one.
A booking must have at least one traveling passenger; a booking without a tour must use the dedicated 'booking without tour' type.

Customers can create bookings directly from the public site/widget with no login required; staff create bookings from the admin; external partners can create FIT bookings via a company auth token integration.

A booking can be placed on a Waitlist when the tour/room is full; accepting a waitlist booking re-checks room inventory availability, consumes the inventory/pickup-location/vehicle seats, applies any coupon, and moves the booking to Booked — rejecting waitlist acceptance if inventory is no longer available. Rejecting a waitlist booking cancels it outright.

Cancelling a booking releases the tour's passenger capacity, pickup-location seats, room-type inventory, assigned vehicle seats, and any held room slots; deletes ticket assignments; processes a refund of whatever was paid minus the cancellation fee (if that's a positive amount); and emails both the customer and staff.
A yacht booking (not manually added) is also cancelled/confirmed in the external yacht reservation source (one of two supported providers) as part of the booking's cancel/payment-confirmation flow.
Once payment is received, a Pending booking automatically transitions to Booked.

rules.fact: A booking's departure and arrival locations must differ from each other (when both are set).
A payment amount is only accepted if the booking still has a balance due, the amount doesn't exceed that balance, and the amount is greater than zero.
A refund amount is only accepted if the booking has any payment recorded, the amount doesn't exceed the total paid, and the amount is greater than zero.

A booking carries its own booking fee percentage (defaulting to 40%, mirroring the tour's default), a second/balance payment portion, and a cancellation fee percentage — each can override the tour-level defaults per booking.
A booking can be flagged for dynamic cancellation pricing instead of a flat cancellation fee — mirroring the same option on the Tours feature.

validations.fact: Creating a booking with more than one passenger marked as the booking client is rejected with 'Multiple booking clients found. Only one client is allowed.'; zero is rejected with 'Client not found in booking.'
A booking with no traveling passenger is rejected with 'At least one traveling passenger is required.'

A payment is rejected if the booking has nothing due ('The booking fee has already been paid.'), if it exceeds the remaining balance ('The amount exceeds the total cost of the tour.'), or if it isn't a positive amount.
Marking a booking fully paid is rejected if it's already fully paid, or if it's only partially paid (staff must record the remaining balance as a partial payment instead).
A refund is rejected if the booking has no payment on record, exceeds what was actually paid, or isn't a positive amount.

permissions.fact: Staff booking management (list, view, create, update, cancel, transfer, coupon application, payment deadline updates) requires authentication plus Django model permissions.
Public booking creation requires no authentication at all, open to any customer.
External FIT bookings (a B2B integration) authenticate via a dedicated company auth token, not a staff login.
Admin sync operations use API-key authentication rather than a staff login, implying a system/scheduled caller.

field_meanings.fact: booking_status distinguishes Booked, Cancelled, Pending, Quote Cancelled, and Waitlist — Waitlist bookings reuse the quote-status field to track their acceptance/rejection since they follow the same flow as a quote once accepted.
due is the remaining balance still owed on a booking; total_payment is what's actually been paid so far; grand_total is the final price after discounts.
is_draft marks a booking that hasn't been finalized/confirmed yet, distinct from its booking_status.

journeys.fact: A customer books a tour, hotel room, or yacht on the public site with no account required, naming exactly one of the travelling passengers as the booking contact; if capacity is full they're placed on a waitlist and notified if/when a spot opens.

A customer or staff member cancels a booking; the customer receives a cancellation email, staff are notified internally, and whatever was paid (minus any cancellation fee) is automatically queued for refund.

side_effects.fact: Cancelling a booking touches five other features' state in one step: Tours (capacity), Hotels (room-type inventory), pickup locations, vehicle assignment, and ticketing (assigned tickets deleted).
Accepting a waitlisted booking applies any attached coupon's usage tracking and creates the booking confirmation voucher/email, same as a normal booking confirmation.

features.name: Passengers
features.summary: Passenger and co-passenger records, bulk passenger import.

workflows.fact: Staff create a passenger record via a form; if the email is already used by another passenger, creation is blocked with an error before anything is saved.
Staff can list/search passengers with filters, paginated.
Staff edit an existing passenger's full record; email uniqueness is re-checked (excluding the passenger being edited).
There is no hard delete for a passenger record; passengers are deactivated instead via a status toggle.
Deactivating/reactivating a passenger is blocked if the acting user is trying to change their own linked passenger record.
Deactivating or reactivating a passenger also flips the linked login account's active status to match, if that passenger has portal access.
If a passenger is matched by email during a booking flow and found inactive, they are automatically reactivated (and their linked login re-activated too).
Staff can export the full passenger/client list to an Excel spreadsheet, respecting the same filters as the list view.
Staff can download a blank Excel import template pre-filled with column headers, a translation row, and one example row, plus an instructions sheet.
Staff can bulk-upload a filled-in Excel file to create many passengers at once in a single request.
Bulk import validates the file itself first (type and size) before opening it.
Bulk import checks that the two mandatory columns exist in the sheet before processing any rows.
Bulk import processes each data row independently: a problem in one row does not stop the rest of the file from importing.
A row whose email already belongs to an existing passenger is skipped (not treated as an error).
Every bulk import upload is recorded as an import-file entry, tracking whether at least one passenger was successfully created from it.
When a booking includes travelers other than the lead passenger, each of those travelers is automatically saved as a reusable 'co-passenger' contact under the lead passenger's account.

rules.fact: A passenger's email must be unique system-wide when set; multiple passengers may have no email at all.
Duplicate email at direct create/edit returns the message 'Client email already exists! Please try a new one.'
Bulk import requires only First Name and Last Name; all ~29 other columns are optional.
Bulk import files must be .xlsx format and no larger than 10 MB.
In the import template, Excel row 1 is the English header, row 2 is a Swedish translation row that must be kept, and actual data starts at row 3.
Salutation is one of Mr, Mrs, or Ms.
Gender is one of Male or Female.
During import, an unrecognized salutation or gender value is left blank rather than rejecting the row.
Import dates should be in YYYY-MM-DD format; a few common alternate formats (DD-MM-YYYY, MM/DD/YYYY, DD/MM/YYYY) are also accepted; anything else that was actually filled in is rejected as invalid.
Organizations and tags referenced during import must already exist in the system; unrecognized ones are silently skipped rather than created or flagged.
Passengers created through bulk import are always categorized as passenger type 'Standard'.
A staff member cannot deactivate or reactivate their own linked passenger record.
The combined address field is built from two underlying address lines joined by a comma, and editing it splits the value back into those two lines.

validations.fact: Uploading no file returns 'No file provided.'
Uploading a non-.xlsx file returns 'Invalid file type. Allowed: .xlsx'
Uploading a file over 10 MB returns 'File too large. Maximum size: 10.0 MB'
A sheet missing First Name or Last Name columns entirely returns 'Missing required columns: ...'
A blank First Name on a row returns row error 'first_name is required'; same pattern for Last Name.
An invalid email format on a row returns 'Invalid email format: {value}'
An email already used by an existing passenger returns 'Email already exists: {value}' and the row is skipped rather than failed.
An unparseable Date of Birth or Passport Expiry Date (when a value was actually entered) returns 'Invalid date_of_birth format: {value}' or 'Invalid passport_expiry_date format: {value}'.
Leaving email blank is always valid, both when creating directly and when importing.
The status-update action requires an explicit active/inactive value; omitting it returns "'is_active' field is required."

permissions.fact: Creating, viewing, editing, deactivating, and exporting passengers all require the user to be logged in and hold the corresponding passenger permission (add/change/view).
Downloading the import template and running a bulk import only require being logged in, not a specific passenger-management permission.
No staff member can change the active/inactive status of the passenger record linked to their own account.

field_meanings.fact: First Name / Last Name — the passenger's everyday given and family name, required.
Email — the passenger's unique contact email; used to detect the same client across separate bookings and imports.
Salutation — Mr, Mrs, or Ms.
Address, Post Code, City — home/mailing address; Address is shown and edited as one combined field.
Gender — Male or Female.
Date of Birth — the passenger's birthdate.
National ID Number — the passenger's national identity/personnummer.
Passport Number / Passport Expiry Date — the passenger's travel document identifiers and validity.
Passport Name (Given Name / Surname) — the name exactly as printed on the passport, kept separate from the everyday First/Last Name.
Passport Birth City — city of birth as shown on the passport.
Nationality — the passenger's nationality/citizenship.
Telephone Number — the passenger's primary contact phone number.
Allergy / Allergy Description — whether the passenger has a known allergy and a free-text description.
Additional Information — free-text notes relevant to the passenger's travel (e.g. meal preference).
Emergency Contact Name / Telephone / Email / Relation — next-of-kin contact details.
Preferred Language, Currency, Country of Residence — the passenger's communication and billing preferences.
Newsletter Subscription (and date) — whether the passenger has opted into marketing communication, and when.
Organizations — companies or organizations this passenger is associated with (e.g. a corporate travel client).
Linked Account — the login account this passenger uses to access the customer portal, if any; deactivating one deactivates the other.
Tags — free-form labels used to categorize passengers (e.g. 'VIP', 'Frequent').

Active/Inactive Status (with changed-by and changed-at) — whether the passenger record is active; deactivating is the only form of 'deleting' a passenger, and every change is logged with who did it and when.

A Co-Passenger is a separate, lightweight 'known traveler' entry saved under a customer's own account, distinct from the master Passenger/client record — used to speed up adding the same travel companions to future bookings.

On a specific booking, each traveler is one Booking Passenger record, separate from the standalone Passenger/client record it may be linked to; it marks whether that person is the primary passenger, whether they are the paying booking client, and whether they are actually traveling.

journeys.fact: To add one passenger: staff open the new-passenger form, fill in at minimum First Name and Last Name; if the email they enter is already used, they see an error and must change it before the record saves.

To bulk-add passengers: staff first download the import template (an Excel file with an English header row, a Swedish translation row, and one filled-in example row, plus a separate instructions sheet explaining formats), delete the example row, fill in their real data starting at row 3, and keep the translation row untouched.
They upload the completed file; if it isn't a .xlsx or is over 10MB, or the required columns are missing entirely, the whole upload is rejected immediately with a specific message.

Otherwise the file is processed row by row and the user is shown a summary: how many rows succeeded, how many were skipped (duplicate emails), how many failed with an error message for each failed row.
To edit a passenger: staff open the passenger's detail record and update any field; changing the email re-runs the same duplicate check used at creation.

To remove a passenger: staff toggle it to inactive rather than deleting it outright; they cannot do this to their own linked passenger record, and if that passenger has portal login access, the login is deactivated in the same action.

To get a spreadsheet of all clients: staff use the export action, which produces a 20-column report covering identity, contact, passport, allergy, emergency-contact, and customer-ID details for the currently filtered list.

side_effects.fact: Adding travelers to a booking reuses an existing passenger record by matching email, and creates a new one only if there's no match — so the same client across multiple bookings stays as one passenger record.
If a matched passenger was inactive, adding them to a new booking automatically reactivates them (and their login, if linked).

Booking travelers other than the lead passenger are automatically saved into the lead passenger's own reusable co-passenger contact list, so the same travel companions can be reused on future bookings.
Adding an organization tag or passenger tag that doesn't already exist under the passenger category creates that tag on the fly.
Booking travelers can be linked to a flight ticket/PNR record, tying passenger identity into ticketing.
Booking travelers can be assigned to a specific tour vehicle seat and a room/room-type, tying passenger identity into tour logistics.

features.name: Flights & Ticketing (PNR) — Overview
features.summary: Overview of PNR/flight-ticket records and how they get linked to bookings; see child docs for detail.

workflows.fact: A PNR/flight-ticket record is created, imported, or synced independently of any booking, then linked to a booking to reserve and assign seats to passengers.

field_meanings.fact: PNR — a single flight-ticket booking reference (from an airline/GDS or entered manually) that can be linked to one or more bookings.

features.name: PNR & Ticket Records
features.summary: Creating and maintaining flight PNRs/tickets: manual entry, bulk Excel import, GDS sync, deadlines/reminders, duplicate merging, error PNRs, and flight arrivals/departures reports.

workflows.fact: Staff upload an Excel file of flight bookings; the system creates or updates the PNR and its flight segments in one pass, and schedules a deadline-reminder email if the PNR has reminder settings.

A bad upload (missing required columns, missing values, bad time format, inconsistent PNR data across rows, or an unknown billing supplier) is rejected with a message naming the exact problem, and none of that file's data is saved.
Staff can create or edit a PNR manually (not via Excel), entering flight segments, named passengers, and individual ticket lines directly.
A PNR that originated from an automatic GDS sync can only have its deadline and flight-segment remarks edited manually; every other field is locked because the GDS feed owns it.

If a newly created or updated PNR turns out to duplicate another PNR with the same reference code and identical flight segments, the system merges them automatically: ticket counts are combined, any bookings using the duplicate are repointed to the surviving PNR, and the duplicate is removed.
When an automatic sync from the airline/GDS system fails, the failure is recorded as an error PNR that staff can review.
Staff view a list of error PNRs; by default only unresolved ones are shown, but filtering by any status (including resolved) switches to showing every error PNR regardless of status.
Staff can run a flight arrivals or departures report for chosen airports and a date range, downloaded as an Excel file listing every affected passenger.
Staff can download a ready-made Excel template for bulk PNR upload, with example data and an instructions sheet.
Staff manage the list of ticket suppliers (airlines) and can deactivate one, unless it's still tied to an active flight segment.

rules.fact: Bulk-uploaded ticket files must be under 5 MB.

A bulk-import row needs values for PNR reference, whether it's a group PNR, passenger count, departure and destination, departure/arrival dates, and departure/arrival times, plus the supplier — all of these are mandatory.
Within one PNR's uploaded rows, the group-PNR flag, passenger count, supplier, and deadline-days value must all match across every row for that PNR, or the upload is rejected.
A deadline reminder email is only scheduled if the PNR has all three of a reminder-days value, a deadline date, and a reminder email address set.
The reminder is sent reminder-days before the deadline; if that date has already passed, it's sent on the deadline date instead.
Setting a reminder requires a deadline to already be set, and the computed reminder date can't be in the past.
A ticket can be Issued, Void, or Refunded; voiding only changes the status, and refunding one ticket line automatically marks every other line sharing the same PNR and ticket number as Refunded too.
Seat/ticket counts never go negative — reducing an allocation below zero is floored at zero instead of erroring.
A ticket supplier's name must be unique, and a URL-friendly identifier is generated for it automatically from the name.
A ticket supplier can't be deactivated while any active flight segment on an active ticket still uses it.

An error PNR is tracked separately per combination of PNR reference, source system, and status — so the same PNR can have more than one open error if it fails for different reasons or from different systems.
An error PNR's status is one of: failed to retrieve, in the error queue, or resolved; the source system is either Amadeus or Sabre.

validations.fact: No file, or a missing file name, on upload returns "This field is required."
A file over the size limit returns "File too large. Maximum allowed size is 5MB."

A sheet missing a required column returns "Missing required columns: {list}"; an empty sheet returns "No rows found"; a row missing a required value returns "Missing required values in column: {column}".
A badly formatted departure/arrival time returns "Invalid time format in column '{column}' at row {row}."
Inconsistent group/passenger-count/supplier/deadline data across a PNR's rows returns "Inconsistent PNR data for PNR: {pnr}..."
A billing supplier that doesn't already exist in the system returns "Supplier '{name}' does not exist. Please create it first."
Manually entering a flight segment without a departure or arrival time returns "Departure time is required." / "Arrival time is required."
Setting the same location as both departure and destination on a segment returns "You cannot select the same location as both the departure and destination."
Attempting to set a reminder with no deadline yet on the ticket returns "Please Update Ticket Deadline."; a reminder date in the past returns "Reminder emails cannot be set before today's date."
Trying to deactivate a ticket supplier still linked to an active flight segment returns "This ticket supplier has active ticket".
Choosing an arrivals/departures report date range where the end date is before the start date is rejected ("...date from cannot be after...date to.").

permissions.fact: Uploading a bulk ticket Excel file only requires being logged in — no specific ticket-management permission is checked.
Viewing the PNR list and the error-PNR list requires being logged in and holding the corresponding view permission.
Downloading the bulk-import template only requires being logged in.
Managing ticket suppliers requires being logged in and holding the corresponding add/change permission; deleting a supplier isn't offered at all (only deactivating one is).
Ticket types can only be viewed by regular staff — creating or editing them is only possible from the platform's central administration console.

field_meanings.fact: PNR Reference — the airline/GDS booking reference code for this ticket record.
Source — whether the PNR was synced automatically from the airline/GDS system or entered manually by staff.
Upload Method — how the PNR entered the system: bulk Excel upload, manual entry, or automatic GDS sync.
Total Tickets / Allocated Tickets — how many seats the PNR holds in total, and how many of those are already reserved against bookings; the remainder is what's still available.
Group PNR — marks a PNR as a block/group booking of shared seats rather than individually tracked passenger tickets.
Deadline, Reminder Days, Reminder Email — when action (e.g. ticketing) is due, how many days beforehand to send a reminder, and who receives it.
Departure/Destination — the overall trip's starting and final point, worked out automatically from the individual flight segments.
Flight Segment (Itinerary) fields — flight number, departure/arrival airport, date and time, carrier, cabin class, number of stops, and aircraft type for one leg of the trip.
Named Passenger (PNR Passenger) — a traveler's name, type (e.g. adult/child), date of birth, and how many tickets they hold on this PNR.
Ticket Line (PNR Ticket) — one issued e-ticket: ticket number, traveler name, fare amounts, carrier, issue date, and its status (Issued, Void, or Refund).
Ticket Supplier — the airline or ticketing supplier a flight segment's ticket was bought through.
Error PNR status — Failed to Retrieve (the initial automatic fetch didn't work), In Error Queue (waiting on retry), or Resolved.

journeys.fact: To bulk-import flights: staff download the template (English headers, an example row to delete, and an instructions sheet), fill in the required columns, and upload it; a bad file is rejected up front with a message pointing at the exact problem, otherwise the PNRs and their flight segments are created or updated, and any deadline reminders are scheduled automatically.

To enter a PNR by hand: staff fill in the flight segments, passengers, and ticket details directly; if it turns out to duplicate an existing PNR with the same reference and identical flights, the system quietly merges them so no duplicate record is left behind.
For a PNR that came from an automatic GDS sync, staff can only adjust its deadline and add remarks to its flight segments — everything else stays under GDS control.
When an automatic sync fails, staff see it appear in the error-PNR list (unresolved ones shown by default) so it can be investigated.

To check who's arriving or departing on a given day: staff pick airports and a date range and download an Excel report listing every affected passenger, whether their flight came from a synced PNR or was added manually.

side_effects.fact: Deactivating a PNR (soft-deleting it) also cancels any scheduled deadline-reminder email tied to it.
Merging a duplicate PNR repoints any bookings that had reserved seats on the duplicate over to the surviving PNR, so no booking loses its flight reservation.
Bulk Excel import can automatically create a new ticket supplier record if the airline name in the file isn't recognized yet.
A PNR's billing supplier is used to determine who to bill for its ticket cost.
Updating a manually-entered (non-GDS) PNR pushes the new flight-segment data into every booking that has reserved seats on it, keeping each booking's own itinerary display in sync.

features.name: Booking Flight Assignment
features.summary: Linking a PNR to a booking, reserving and assigning seats to passengers, keeping a booking's flight segments in sync with its PNR, and removing a PNR from a booking.

workflows.fact: Staff reserve a number of seats from a PNR against a confirmed booking; this only works while the booking is in Booked status, the PNR is active, and there are enough unreserved seats and transport-needing passengers to cover the request.
Reserving seats on a booking also copies the PNR's current flight segments onto the booking so its own itinerary display is populated immediately.
Staff assign one reserved seat to a specific traveling passenger on the booking; a passenger can only be assigned once per reservation, and a passenger not on that booking can't be picked.
Staff can reassign an already-assigned seat to a different passenger, or unassign it outright; both actions keep the reservation's assigned-seat count accurate.
When a reservation's seat count exactly matches the booking's passenger count, staff can assign every traveling passenger in one action instead of one at a time.
A seat reservation can't be removed once any passenger has been assigned to it — staff must unassign passengers first.
Staff can trigger a manual "recreate segments" action on a booking's linked PNR to re-sync its flight segments if they look stale or incomplete.
A scheduled background process finds bookings whose linked PNR has flight segments that never made it onto the booking, and re-syncs them automatically.
Removing a PNR from a booking is blocked entirely if any billing has already been generated from its flight segments.
Staff can download a passenger manifest for a specific ticket reservation, or for a date/airport range, listing every assigned traveler and their passport/contact details.

rules.fact: A reservation can't be for more seats than the PNR still has available, nor more than the number of passengers on the booking who still need transport.
Only one seat reservation is allowed per booking-and-PNR combination — a second attempt is rejected.
Reducing an already-made reservation's seat count can't drop it below the number of passengers already assigned to it, nor exceed the booking's total passenger count.
Only one passenger can be assigned per seat reservation slot — the same passenger can't be assigned twice to the same reservation, and the same seat slot can't hold two passengers.
Passengers marked as free-travel on tour and non-tour bookings don't count against the reservation's assigned-seat total; on yacht bookings every assigned passenger always counts.

One-click group assignment only works when the reservation's seat count, the number of passengers needing transport, and the booking's total passenger count are all exactly equal — any mismatch, or an already-fully-assigned reservation, blocks the action.

When a booking's flight segments are re-synced from its PNR, existing segments are matched to the PNR's current segments by flight order; any segment no longer present is removed, but if it already had billing attached, that billing is carried over to another segment instead of being lost, and removal is skipped if there's nowhere to move the billing.
Removing a PNR from a booking is refused outright if any billing line exists on its flight segments — issued or not — and refused with a more specific message if that billing has already been issued.

Removing a PNR from a booking also removes any traveling passenger who only existed because of that PNR, and adjusts the booking's passenger count accordingly for bookings made without a tour package.

If a booking's flight cost changes after a re-sync, the booking's totals and balance due are recalculated automatically, and both an increase and a decrease trigger a notification to the accounting system.
A booking's return date can be set automatically from its flight data, but only for bookings made without a tour package, and only if it hasn't already been manually set.

validations.fact: Reserving or group-assigning seats on a booking that isn't in Booked status is rejected: "Can't assign tickets on cancelled, transferred and pending booking!"
Reserving seats on an inactive PNR is rejected: "This ticket is not active."
Reserving more seats than the PNR has left is rejected: "There are not enough tickets on this ticket to allocate to this booking."
Requesting more seats than passengers who still need transport is rejected: "You can't assign more tickets than total transport required for passengers"
A duplicate seat reservation for the same booking and PNR is rejected: "Same booking ticket exists."
Trying to remove a reservation that already has assigned passengers is rejected: "This booking ticket is already used."
Assigning a seat to a passenger not on that booking is rejected: "This passenger is not from this booking."
Assigning a passenger twice to the same reservation is rejected: "You have already assigned the same ticket to this booking passenger."

Group-assigning when the counts don't line up exactly is rejected: "Passenger count does not match. Group assign is not possible."; attempting it when already fully assigned is rejected: "Ticket assignment for all passenger completed!"
Recreating a PNR's flight segments on a booking where that PNR isn't actually linked is rejected: "PNR is not linked to this booking."

Removing a PNR from a booking is rejected outright if any billing line is attached to its flight segments ("Cannot delete PNR as there are financial lines linked to the itinerary segments."), and specifically if that billing was already issued ("The corresponding PNR billing line is already issued and cannot be deleted.").

permissions.fact: Reserving seats from a PNR, assigning/reassigning/unassigning passengers, group-assigning, and downloading passenger manifests all only require the staff member to be logged in — no dedicated permission beyond that.
Recreating a booking's flight segments and viewing/removing a booking's linked PNR require being logged in and holding the relevant permission.
The scheduled bulk re-sync of booking flight segments is a system/service action, not something a staff member triggers directly through the normal login.

field_meanings.fact: Reserved Seats / Assigned Seats — how many seats a booking has reserved from a PNR, and how many of those have actually been given to a named passenger so far.
Seat Assignment — the link between one reserved seat and the specific traveling passenger it belongs to.

Booking's Flight Segment — a copy of a PNR's flight-leg details (times, airports, carrier) kept on the booking itself, so viewing or printing a booking's itinerary doesn't depend on the master PNR staying unchanged.
Show in Itinerary — lets staff hide a flight segment from the customer-facing itinerary/printout without deleting it from the booking.
Manually Added — marks a flight segment or ticket line that a staff member entered directly on the booking, rather than one that came from syncing a PNR.

journeys.fact: To get a passenger flying: staff first reserve however many seats they need from an active PNR against the confirmed booking (blocked if the booking isn't Booked, the PNR is inactive, or there aren't enough seats/passengers to justify it) — this also fills in the booking's own flight-segment display right away.
Staff then assign each traveling passenger to one of the reserved seats one at a time, or — if the numbers line up exactly — assign everyone in a single group action instead.
If a passenger's seat needs to change, staff reassign it directly; to free up a seat entirely, staff unassign the passenger first, since a reservation with any assigned passenger can't be deleted.

If the master PNR's flight details change later, staff can trigger a manual re-sync ("recreate segments") on the booking to bring its flight display back in line, or wait for the scheduled background process to catch bookings that were missed.

To remove a flight from a booking entirely, staff remove the linked PNR — but this is refused if any billing has already been created from those flight segments, so staff need to resolve the billing first.

side_effects.fact: A change in a booking's flight cost after re-syncing automatically updates the booking's total and balance due, and notifies the accounting system of the increase or decrease.
A flight-cost change can also adjust the travel agent's commission on the booking.
Removing a PNR from a booking removes any traveling passenger that only existed for that PNR, and unlinks any other traveler still referencing it.
Removing a PNR's flight segments also updates any bundled itinerary package those segments belonged to.
For bookings made without a tour package, a booking's return date can be automatically filled in from its flight data.

features.name: Tours
features.summary: Tour catalog: tours with pricing, room types, supplements, discounts, pickup locations and vehicles.

workflows.fact: Staff create a tour via TourAPIViewSet (POST); the departure_date, capacity, and standard_price are required at creation, base_standard_price is set equal to standard_price at creation time, and a slug is generated from name + id + departure_date.

Creating a tour also creates its passenger-type records, its default-language multilanguage record, applies a default pickup location (and a pickup-request location if the tenant allows requested pickups), sets local prices, and sends an admin new-tour-notification email.
A tour can be created as a 'repeat' of an existing tour (repeat_tour), which copies images, syncs translations, and carries over the source tour's default_profile if none is given.

Activating/deactivating a tour (update_status) is blocked with a specific error if the tour has an active booking, an active waitlist booking, any inactive supplements attached, or assigned tour guides — staff must resolve each condition first.
Deactivating a tour releases its held room types back into general inventory.

A scheduled job (UpdateDepartedTourStatusSchedulerAPIView, API-key auth) marks tours with a past departure_date as departed, marks their booked passengers as departed, and applies the tour's tag to those passengers.

A scheduled job (RemoveTourReservationSchedulerAPIView, API-key auth) finds active, non-departed tours whose reservation_expiry_date has passed and clears the reservation hold (is_reserved, reserved_capacity, reservation_expiry_date), then recalculates remaining_capacity.
Draft status can also be toggled via a dedicated API-key-authenticated endpoint (TourDraftUpdateAPIView) independent of the main update flow.

rules.fact: A tour's standard_price must be greater than or equal to its transfer_price (transport cost) — zero-priced tours are explicitly allowed, but the tour price can never be cheaper than the transfer cost.

When the tenant's 'beetroot_pricing' add-on is active, both base_standard_price and standard_price must fall within the tour's configured min_standard_price/max_standard_price bounds, each checked independently with its own error message.

Setting a tour to draft (is_draft=True) always forces it inactive (is_active=False); taking it out of draft always forces it active — draft and active status are mutually coupled, both at creation and via the dedicated draft-toggle endpoint.

The default booking fee is 40% of the tour price (booking_fee_percent default), with payment_fee_type deciding whether fees are calculated as a percentage or a fixed amount; a second_payment_percent/second_payment_amount governs the balance-due portion.

A tour can price its cancellation either as a static cancel_fee/cancel_fee_percent, or opt into dynamic cancellation pricing (is_dynamic_cancellation) — the dynamic calculation itself is part of the Booking feature's cancellation logic, not the tour record.

Public/customer-facing tour listings only show a tour if it has no allowed_hosts restriction (visible on every brand) or the requesting domain is explicitly in its allowed_hosts — this is the multi-brand visibility gate for the booking widget and public site.

validations.fact: Creating/updating a tour rejects a standard_price below transfer_price with 'Tour Standard price must be greater than or equal to transport cost.'

With beetroot_pricing active, a base_standard_price or standard_price outside the tour's min/max_standard_price bounds is rejected with a distinct message per bound violated (four separate checks: base below min, base above max, price below min, price above max).

Attempting to activate/deactivate a tour with an active booking, active waitlist booking, inactive supplements, or assigned tour guides is rejected with a message naming exactly which condition is blocking it.

permissions.fact: Staff tour CRUD (TourAPIViewSet) requires authentication plus Django model permissions (add/change/delete_tour) — standard staff-role gating.

Public tour browsing (PublicTourViewSet, availability, search, room-type preview) has no authentication requirement — open to anyone, gated only by the allowed_hosts domain filter above, not by login.

Scheduled/system operations (departure status rollover, reservation-hold expiry, draft toggling) are gated by API-key authentication rather than a staff login, implying they're driven by a scheduler or external caller rather than the admin UI.
Bulk tour updates (TourBulkUpdateAPIView) require authentication plus Django model permissions, same tier as regular staff CRUD.

field_meanings.fact: is_reserved / reserved_capacity / reservation_expiry_date together represent a temporary capacity hold on a tour (e.g. while a booking is in progress) that auto-expires and releases back to remaining_capacity if not confirmed by the expiry date.
is_departed marks a tour whose departure_date has passed and whose status rollover job has run; it does not mean the tour was deleted or cancelled.
is_allotment_tour marks tours that sell room-type inventory in bulk allotments rather than per-passenger capacity alone (works together with the Hotels/Accommodation room-type inventory).
default_profile scopes which company/tenant 'profile' (a multi-brand/multi-office concept) a tour belongs to by default when synced or repeated.

journeys.fact: A customer browsing the public site or widget sees only tours visible on that domain (per the allowed_hosts rule) with available capacity; opening a tour shows its images, pricing, supplements, pickup locations, room types, discounts, and tags via the public tour endpoint.

Staff create a tour in the admin, optionally as a repeat of a past tour to save re-entering details; the tour can be left as a draft (invisible/inactive) until ready, then published by clearing draft status.
As departure day passes, the system automatically marks the tour and its passengers departed with no manual step required from staff.

side_effects.fact: Creating a tour triggers an admin email notification, creates passenger-type and multilanguage records for the tour, applies default/requested pickup locations, and sets local prices — all as part of the same create step.
Deactivating a tour releases its reserved room-type inventory back to the shared pool (cross-references the Hotels/Accommodation feature's room-type inventory).
A tour's price and discount changes are tracked in TourDiscountHistory, giving an audit trail of price/discount changes over time.

features.name: Tour Types
features.summary: Reusable tour templates (type, images, vehicles, pickup locations) that tours are built from.

workflows.fact: Staff create a Tour Type template with core commercial details (name, price, duration, capacity, currency, territory/location, fee structure), plus optional pickup locations, vehicle assignments, and images, all in one submission.
Creating a tour type automatically adds a default pickup location, and also a 'request pickup' option if the tenant allows pickup requests.
Creating or editing a tour type automatically creates or updates a matching translation record in the tenant's default language, mirroring the name, description, and tour information just entered.
Staff can upload images to a tour type after it's created; the very first image uploaded automatically becomes the main/cover image.
Staff can delete an image; if it was the main image, another remaining image is automatically promoted to take its place.
Staff can explicitly set which image is the main/cover image for a tour type.
Staff can add translations of a tour type one language at a time; requesting a translation for a language that hasn't been added yet returns an empty result rather than an error.

Staff can assign specific vehicles to a tour type with their own per-vehicle seat capacity, separate from a simpler general vehicle list; any vehicle previously assigned but left out of a later update is removed.
Staff can retire a specific vehicle assignment on a tour type without deleting it outright.
Editing an existing tour type recalculates its fees and re-validates pickup-location capacity, and removes any pickup location or vehicle assignment no longer included in the update.
A tour type can't be deactivated while any active Tour is still built from it.
A separate central-administration process (not a regular staff login) can also manage tour types system-wide, for platform-level configuration.

rules.fact: The standard price must be greater than or equal to the transfer (transport) price.

Fees can be calculated as a percentage of the standard price, a fixed flat amount, or a fixed amount per passenger; percentage is the default, and the default booking fee is 40% of the standard price.

When fees are percentage-based, the booking fee, second payment, cancellation fee, and travel insurance fee are each calculated from the standard price and rounded to a whole number; when a flat fee type is used instead, those amounts are taken directly as entered.
If no VAT class is specified, tour types default to "No VAT".

The total seats assigned across all of a tour type's pickup locations can't exceed the tour type's overall capacity — for example, a tour type with a capacity of 20 can't have pickup locations adding up to 25 seats.

Each pickup location on a tour type starts out with all of its seats available; saving the tour type's pickup-location configuration again resets availability back to the full seat count for every pickup location.
A vehicle can only be assigned once to a given tour type, and a translation can only be added once per language per tour type.
Leaving a vehicle assignment's seat capacity at 0 means it inherits the vehicle's own default capacity rather than literally offering zero seats.
Supplements, vehicles, and accommodations assigned to a tour type must all be active — inactive ones are rejected.
Only one image per tour type can be the main/cover image at any time.

validations.fact: Creating a tour type without its core details returns "No meta_data provided."
A standard price lower than the transfer price returns "Standard price must be greater than or equal to transport cost."
Assigning an inactive supplement, vehicle, or accommodation returns "Supplement must be active!", "Vehicle must be active!", or "Accommodation must be active!" respectively.
An inactive pickup location, a negative pickup-location price, or a negative pickup-location seat count are each rejected with a specific message naming the problem.
Pickup-location seats adding up to more than the tour type's capacity returns "Pickup Location total seats assigned ({total}) exceeds capacity ({capacity})."
Adding a translation in an inactive language returns "Language is not valid."
Requesting a translation without specifying which language returns "Language code is required".
Uploading an image to a deactivated tour type returns "Invalid Tour-type".
Trying to delete an image through the wrong tour type's page returns "This image is from another tour-type."
Trying to deactivate a tour type still used by an active Tour returns "This template is used in active tour."
Uploaded images are checked for file size and image type; an oversized or invalid image file is rejected.

permissions.fact: Creating, viewing, and editing tour types, their translations, and their vehicle assignments all require the staff member to be logged in and hold the corresponding permission; tour types can't be deleted outright, only deactivated.
A public, unauthenticated listing exists that shows only active tour types with minimal public-facing details, for use on customer-facing pages.
Managing tour types from the platform's central administration console uses a separate system-level authorization, not a normal staff login.

field_meanings.fact: Name / Description / Tour Information — the tour template's default-language display name, description, and operational information shown to staff and customers.
Duration — the length of the tour.
Capacity — the maximum total number of passengers this tour template supports, used to cap how many pickup-location seats can be assigned.
Standard Price / Transfer Price — the base price for the tour, and the portion of that price allocated to transport; the standard price can never be lower than the transfer price.
Fee Type — whether booking, second-payment, cancellation, and travel-insurance fees are calculated as a percentage of the price or as flat amounts.
Booking Fee, Second Payment, Cancellation Fee, Travel Insurance Fee — the calculated deposit, balance payment, cancellation charge, and insurance charge for tours built from this template.
Territory / Country / Location — where the tour operates geographically.
Supplements — optional paid add-ons customers can book alongside a tour of this type.
Accommodations — hotel/lodging options linked to this tour type.
VAT Class — the tax classification applied to this tour type's pricing; defaults to "No VAT" if not set.
Allowed Hosts — which whitelabel sites/domains are permitted to show and sell this tour type.
Tour Description URL — an external web page with more marketing detail about the tour.
Pickup Location, Price, Seats, Remaining Seats — a specific pickup point available for the tour, any extra price for choosing it, how many seats are allocated there, and how many are still available.
Vehicle Assignment (Capacity, Active) — a specific vehicle usable for this tour type, how many seats it provides, and whether the assignment is currently in use.
Translation (Name, Description, Tour Information) — the tour type's content shown to customers in a specific language.
Cost Center / Accounting Project — which internal accounting bucket this tour type's costs and revenue are attributed to.

journeys.fact: To set up a new tour type: staff enter its commercial details (price, capacity, fees, territory) in one go, optionally listing pickup locations, vehicles, and images at the same time; the system fills in a default pickup location automatically and creates a default-language translation entry ready to be translated further.
To build out a tour type's presentation: staff add images afterward — the first one becomes the cover image automatically — and can change the cover image or delete images at any time.
To make a tour type available in more languages: staff add one translation per language; if a language hasn't been translated yet, viewing it simply comes back empty rather than erroring.
To adjust which vehicles serve a tour type: staff assign vehicles with their own seat capacity, and can deactivate a specific vehicle's assignment without removing its configuration entirely.
To retire a tour type: staff deactivate it, which is blocked while any active Tour is still built from that template — the template first needs its dependent tours addressed.

side_effects.fact: A tour type's pricing and fee configuration is recalculated every time it's saved, which is the source new Tours built from that template draw their defaults from.

Resaving a tour type's pickup-location list removes any pickup location no longer included, and resets remaining seats to full for the ones that stay — so previously consumed seat counts are not preserved across an update.
A tour type ties into accounting through its cost center and accounting project fields, connecting it to the platform's financial reporting.
A tour type can be linked to a custom-fields configuration that determines what information is collected during booking and for each passenger.
Deactivating a tour type is blocked while it's still used by an active Tour, protecting live bookings from losing their underlying template.

features.name: Custom Tour Offers
features.summary: Bespoke tour offers with Wetu itinerary import, supplements and pickup locations.

workflows.fact: Staff can import a client's itinerary from Wetu (a third-party itinerary tool), either fetching the full list of booked itineraries at once or refreshing a single one by its identifier.
Staff convert a Wetu itinerary into a Custom Tour Offer in one action, adding the pricing/territory/VAT context Wetu itself doesn't carry; a Wetu itinerary can only be converted once.
Staff can also create a custom offer from scratch without importing anything from Wetu.
Creating an offer automatically links or creates a customer account for the prospective client using their name and email.
Creating an offer automatically adds a default pickup location, and a 'request pickup' option too if the tenant allows pickup requests.
Staff can preview the full cost breakdown of an offer at any time — either using an offer that's already saved, or with raw pricing/capacity/supplement figures before anything is saved at all.
Staff can add internal notes to an offer to track context on the deal; each edit to a note keeps a history of what it said before.
Staff send the offer to the customer as a branded PDF by email, or just download the PDF without emailing it; sending can also happen automatically as part of saving the offer.
Once the customer accepts, staff convert the offer into a real Tour and Booking in one action; this can only be done once per offer.
Staff can duplicate an existing offer to use as a starting point for a similar deal; the copy always starts as an inactive draft.
Customers view their own custom tour offers through the customer portal, scoped only to offers made out to them.

rules.fact: An offer's standard price must be greater than or equal to its transfer price.
The total seats assigned across an offer's pickup locations can't exceed its overall capacity.
The number of passengers taking the paid transfer/pickup can't exceed the offer's total capacity.
The default booking fee is 40% of the standard price unless changed.
If no VAT class is set, an offer defaults to "No VAT".
An offer can only be converted into a Tour and Booking once; converting it deactivates the offer so it can't be converted again.
Only an active offer can be converted into a booking — a deactivated, expired, or already-converted offer can't be.
A discount on the offer is only applied at conversion if the offer is marked as discounted, and can be a flat amount or a percentage of the total price; the applied amount is never less than zero.
A Wetu itinerary can only be converted into a custom offer if it's in "Booked" status in Wetu, and hasn't already been converted.
Only the staff member who created an internal note can edit it later — anyone else attempting to edit it is refused.
Duplicating an offer always produces an inactive draft, regardless of the original offer's status.
If the offer's price is quoted in a different currency than what the customer is billed in, all prices shown to the customer are converted using the offer's exchange rate.
Only one pickup location of each specific pickup point can be added per offer.

validations.fact: A standard price lower than the transfer price returns "Tour Standard price must be greater than or equal to transport cost."
Pickup-location seats adding up to more than capacity returns "Pickup Locations total seats assigned ({total}) exceeds capacity ({capacity})".
An inactive pickup location, negative price, or negative seats on a pickup location are each rejected with a specific message.
An inactive supplement added to an offer returns "Supplement must be active!"
Requesting a cost preview for transfer passengers exceeding total capacity returns "Passenger transfer count cannot exceed total capacity."
Editing a note as anyone other than its creator returns "Only note creator can update a note."
Trying to convert an offer that's already been converted returns "Tour and booking is already created for this custom tour offer".
Trying to convert a Wetu itinerary that's already been converted, or isn't in Booked status, is rejected with a message naming which condition failed.
Converting a Wetu itinerary whose customer name can't be split into a first and last name returns "Customer Name is not compatible for create booking. Please provide firstname and lastname."
Converting a Wetu itinerary whose computed price works out to zero or less returns "Standard price must be greater than 0."

permissions.fact: Creating, editing, listing, converting-to-booking, and status-updating custom tour offers all require staff to be logged in and hold the corresponding permission.
Duplicating an offer and previewing its cost only require being logged in, without a specific permission check.
Importing and converting Wetu itineraries is only available to tenants whose subscription plan includes the Wetu integration feature.
Customers can only see custom tour offers made out to them personally through the customer portal; if a staff member is viewing on a customer's behalf, that view is read-only.

field_meanings.fact: Tour Name / Description / Tour Information — the display name, description, and detailed information about the bespoke tour package shown to the customer.
Duration / Capacity / Departure & Return Date — the trip length in days, how many passengers it's sized for, and the trip's start/end dates.
Standard Price / Transfer Price — the base per-person tour price and the per-person cost of the pickup/transfer option.
Booking Currency / Conversion Rate — the currency the customer is actually charged in, and the exchange rate used to convert the offer's base price into that currency.
Discounted / Discount Type / Discount Amount — whether a discount applies, whether it's a flat amount or a percentage, and its value.
Grand Total — the final calculated total price of the offer after supplements, pickup, transfer, and discount, in the customer's billing currency.
Offer Origin — whether the offer was created directly by staff or generated from an imported Wetu itinerary.
Draft / Active — whether the offer is still being worked on (draft) and whether it's currently usable/convertible (active); an offer is automatically deactivated once converted into a booking.
Tour and Booking Created — whether this offer has already been turned into a real Tour and Booking.
Email Sent — whether the offer has been emailed to the customer at least once.
Duplicated From — a reference back to the original offer this one was copied from, if it's a duplicate.
Note / Edit History — an internal staff comment on the offer, along with a record of everything it said before each edit.
Pickup Location, Price, Seats, Remaining Seats — a specific pickup point offered with this deal, any extra price for it, and how many seats are allotted/available there.
Supplement, Price, Quantity, Mandatory — an add-on included in the offer (e.g. a flight or hotel), its price and quantity, and whether it's required as part of the deal.
Wetu Itinerary Status — the booking status of the itinerary as recorded in Wetu; only an itinerary marked "Booked" there can become a custom tour offer.

journeys.fact: Staff building a custom deal typically start by importing the client's itinerary from Wetu if one exists, then convert it into a custom tour offer, adding pricing, territory, and tax details Wetu doesn't provide.
Staff configure the offer's pricing, pickup locations, and supplements (flights, hotels, extras), checking the running cost total at any point before committing.
Staff send the finished offer to the customer as a branded PDF by email, or download it to share another way.
Once the customer accepts, staff convert the offer directly into a real Tour and Booking in one action — after which the offer itself is locked and can't be converted again.
For a similar future deal, staff can duplicate an existing offer as a starting point rather than rebuilding it from scratch.
The customer can log into their own portal at any time to see the offers made out to them.

side_effects.fact: Converting an offer creates a real, privately-listed Tour carrying over its name, description, dates, capacity, pricing, pickup locations, and supplements.
Converting an offer also creates the actual Booking on that new tour, with the offer's customer as the primary passenger and any discount applied.
Creating an offer can create a brand-new customer account, or upgrade an existing account to have customer-portal access.
Sending an offer dispatches a branded email with a PDF attachment, using the tenant's own logo, colors, and contact details.
The offer's cost preview draws on the same tax/VAT calculations used for bookings, so quoted totals match what an actual booking would charge.

features.name: Hotels & Accommodation
features.summary: Hotels, room types with inventory and pricing, amenities, and room bookings.

workflows.fact: A new hotel is always created inactive; staff must explicitly activate it once it's ready, and activation is blocked unless the hotel has at least one room type added.
Deactivating a hotel is blocked if any of its room types is currently used as allotment inventory on an active tour — staff must remove that dependency first.

Room-type inventory is tracked per date, per room type, split into two pools: a Fixed allotment (contracted rooms) and a Call-off allotment (rooms available on request/on-demand) — each with its own available/booked counts.
When a booking books beds in a room type for a date range, the system books from the Fixed pool first, and only pulls from the Call-off pool once the Fixed pool for that date is exhausted.
Releasing a booking (cancellation/change) reverses that same fixed-first, call-off-second order, freeing beds/rooms back to inventory.
A room type can also be temporarily reserved (held) independent of an actual booking, via increase/update_reserved_rooms, and released the same way tours release capacity holds.

Accommodation records (simple lodging: name, address, description, website) are a lighter-weight alternative to full Hotel/RoomType inventory tracking, and are attached directly to a tour rather than going through the inventory/booking-room system.

rules.fact: A hotel cannot be activated without at least one room type already added to it.
A hotel cannot be deactivated while any of its room types is in active use as tour allotment inventory.

A room type's total available rooms (fixed + call-off) can never be set lower than what's already booked plus reserved against it — validated per date and, for bulk edits, across the whole date range.
Fixed available rooms can never be set below fixed booked rooms, and call-off available rooms can never be set below call-off booked rooms — each pool is validated independently as well as in total.
A reserved-rooms adjustment that would push a room type's reserved count negative is rejected outright.

validations.fact: Activating a hotel with zero room types is rejected with 'At least one room type should be added to activate hotel.'
Deactivating a hotel still in use by an active tour is rejected with "Hotel is used in a tour. You can't deactivate it."
Saving an inventory record whose available rooms would be less than its already-booked-plus-reserved rooms is rejected per date, naming which pool (fixed or call-off) is the problem.

permissions.fact: All hotel and room-type management (list/create/update/activate-deactivate) requires authentication plus Django model permissions — standard staff-role gating, no public access.
Inventory breakdown views require authentication only (no explicit model-permission check beyond being logged in).

field_meanings.fact: Fixed allotment = rooms the business has contractually committed to sell regardless of demand; Call-off allotment = additional rooms available on request beyond the fixed commitment. Both are tracked separately for available and booked counts on every inventory date.
reserved_rooms is a temporary hold on room-type inventory (mirroring the Tours feature's capacity hold), separate from an actual confirmed booking.
total_available_rooms (a computed property) is fixed + call-off available, minus reserved holds and total booked rooms — the number actually sellable right now for that date.
price_type on a room type determines whether its price is calculated per person or as a flat room rate.

journeys.fact: Staff add a hotel (created inactive by default), attach its room types and inventory, then activate it once at least one room type exists — from then on it's eligible to be used in tour allotments.

When a passenger books a room on a tour, availability is drawn first from the hotel's fixed allotment for those dates, then from call-off inventory if fixed is exhausted; cancelling releases it back in the same order.

side_effects.fact: Booking or releasing room-type inventory recalculates fixed_booked_rooms/call_off_booked_rooms across the whole stay's date range in a single bulk update, not one row at a time.
A hotel's room-type/inventory data feeds tour-side availability calculations shown to staff and, indirectly, to customers via the Tours feature's allotment tours.

features.name: Yacht Booking — Overview
features.summary: Overview of the yacht charter catalog and booking flow; see child docs for detail.

workflows.fact: Yachts are synced in from external charter providers, priced per week, and made available for customers to search and book.

field_meanings.fact: A Yacht is a single chartered boat listed in the catalog, either synced from an external provider or added manually by staff.

features.name: Yacht Catalog & Pricing
features.summary: The yacht charter catalog (yachts, companies, countries, sailing areas, shipyards), manual boat entries, and per-week pricing/discount management, synced from external charter providers.

workflows.fact: Yacht catalog data (yachts, companies, countries, world regions, sailing areas, shipyards, equipment) is regularly synced in from external charter providers rather than entered by hand.
Staff can browse the yacht catalog, filter by provider, and drill into a single yacht to see its full specs, images, add-ons, pickup locations, and finance settings.
Staff manage reference data (world regions, sailing areas, shipyards, countries, companies, equipment) — viewing lists, toggling active/inactive, and triggering a re-sync from the provider.
Staff can add a yacht manually by picking an existing catalog yacht and cloning it into a separate, staff-managed listing that catalog sync will never touch or remove.

Staff view a price sheet for a chartering company, showing each yacht's per-week price and discount for a chosen date range and currency, and can adjust the discount for one yacht or in bulk across a date range.
Pricing and availability are synced in weekly blocks from the external provider, and prices are automatically converted into every active currency the tenant supports.
Staff can edit a yacht's add-on supplements and pickup locations directly, along with its finance/tax settings.
Turning a yacht on updates its listing on the public-facing site immediately and refreshes its availability for the current year right away.

rules.fact: A full catalog sync automatically deactivates any yacht (or other catalog entry) from that provider that's no longer present in the latest sync, unless it was added manually by staff — manually added entries are never touched by sync.
Pricing and availability are always synced in whole-week blocks (Saturday to Saturday).
The price sheet only lists chartering companies that have at least one active yacht, and only shows active, non-manually-added yachts.
Some catalog reference data — pricing measurement units, seasons, and services — is only available through one of the two charter providers; requesting it from the other is rejected outright.
A yacht without a tax classification is automatically given a default one, so no yacht can go unbilled for lack of tax setup.
Availability syncing skips any yacht that's inactive, manually added, or has been removed from the provider's feed.

validations.fact: Viewing the manually-added yachts list without specifying a currency returns "Missing required query parameter(s): currency".
Editing a yacht's supplement without a price, or with a negative price, or with an inactive supplement, is each rejected with a specific message.
Editing a yacht's pickup location with a negative price or a negative seat count is rejected with a specific message.
Requesting price measurements, seasons, services, or yacht models from a provider that doesn't support them returns a message naming exactly what isn't supported.
Triggering a sync with an unrecognized data source returns a message listing which sources are actually supported.

permissions.fact: Viewing and managing the yacht catalog, reference data, manual boats, and price sheets all require staff to be logged in and hold the relevant permission.
Listing a yacht's pickup locations only requires being logged in, without a specific permission check.

field_meanings.fact: Name, Model, Build Year, Shipyard — the yacht's identifying details and who built it.
Kind (Yacht Type) — the category of yacht, such as sailing yacht or catamaran.
Home Base, Chartering Company — the marina the yacht departs/returns from, and the operating company that owns/manages it.
Cabins, Berths, Toilets — the yacht's sleeping and washroom capacity.
Maximum People On Board — the total passenger capacity cap for the yacht.
Minimum/Maximum Charter Duration — the shortest and longest booking length the yacht allows.
Standard Check-In Day/Time and Check-Out Time — the yacht's usual charter turnover schedule.
Equipment — the onboard equipment and amenities available on the yacht.
Manually Added — marks a yacht that staff added by hand rather than one kept in sync with an external provider; such yachts are never auto-deactivated or overwritten by sync.
Removed — marks a yacht that's disappeared from the external provider's feed.
World Region, Country, Sailing Area, Shipyard — the geographic and manufacturer classification used to browse and filter the catalog.
Price, Provider Discount, Staff Discount — a yacht's listed price for a given week, any discount the provider already applied, and an additional discount staff can layer on top.
Available — whether the yacht is actually bookable for a given week, tracked separately from its price.

journeys.fact: Staff browse the synced catalog to see which yachts, companies, and reference data are available, filtering by provider and toggling entries active/inactive as needed.
To offer a yacht outside the normal synced catalog, staff clone it into a manually-added listing that stays under their own control and won't be touched by future syncs.

To set pricing, staff open the price sheet for a chartering company, review each yacht's weekly price and discount for a date range, and adjust the discount for one yacht or across many yachts at once.
Staff fine-tune a yacht's supplements, pickup locations, and tax settings directly on its detail page.

side_effects.fact: Any catalog sync also refreshes the yacht's listing on the external public-facing site, so changes show up there without a separate manual step.
Any pricing sync regenerates prices in every active currency the tenant supports, which is what the booking search and price sheet actually display.
Syncing bases, countries, and yacht types also refreshes their translated names used elsewhere on the storefront.
Every yacht is automatically given a tax classification if it doesn't already have one, so pricing always has a valid tax basis for billing.

features.name: Yacht Search, Booking & Reservation
features.summary: Customer yacht search and booking, cost preview, staff booking management, and confirming/cancelling the reservation with the external charter provider.

workflows.fact: A customer searches for yachts by destination, date, and currency on the public site, sees per-yacht pricing for the searched dates, and can view full details of a single yacht.
A customer requests a cost preview showing the itemized price breakdown, discount, tax, and total due before committing to a booking.
A customer submits the booking directly on the public site without needing an account, or staff create one internally on the customer's behalf.
Before a booking is placed, the system checks live availability with the external charter provider for the exact dates requested; if unavailable, the booking is rejected.
Placing a booking opens a reservation with the actual charter provider; if that fails, the booking is automatically cancelled instead of being left in a broken state.
Staff explicitly confirm a pending booking, which confirms the reservation with the charter provider and marks the booking as booked.
Staff can edit an existing pending or booked yacht booking's passengers, add-ons, and pricing.
Cancelling a yacht booking also cancels the reservation held with the charter provider, unless the booking was entered manually.
A pending booking is automatically cancelled if the customer misses the first payment deadline.
Once a booking's departure date arrives, it's automatically marked as departed and a financial record is sent for accounting.
For yachts crewed through one of the providers, crew is automatically assigned to a booking roughly a day before departure.
Staff can book a yacht that was added manually (not synced from a provider), skipping the live availability check and the external reservation step entirely, using a staff-entered price instead.

rules.fact: A booking can't be placed unless the exact requested date range is confirmed available with the charter provider — unless it's a manually-entered booking, which skips this check.
A manually-entered booking must have its price entered by staff — it isn't calculated automatically.
The number of passengers must be greater than zero, and how many took the paid transfer can't exceed the total passenger count.
A booking must list at least one passenger, and no more passengers than the declared total; each passenger's email must be unique within the booking.
A public (customer-submitted) booking must have exactly one passenger marked as the primary contact, and that passenger must have a valid email.
Only supplements that are currently active can be added to a booking.
A booking's passenger count can never be reduced below the number of passengers already registered on it.

A booking moves from Pending to Booked only once staff explicitly confirm it with the charter provider; it moves to Cancelled if the reservation fails, the payment deadline is missed, or it's cancelled outright.
Payment due dates for a booking come directly from the charter provider's own payment schedule for that reservation.
If a booking's total changes after an edit, both the customer and the accounting system are notified of the increase or decrease.

validations.fact: A cost preview or booking with zero or fewer passengers returns "Number of passengers must be greater than zero."
A transfer passenger count higher than the total passenger count returns a message naming the mismatch.
A manual booking submitted without a price returns "Price must be provided for manual booking."

A booking with no passengers listed returns "Booking must include at least one passenger."; more passengers listed than declared returns a message naming the mismatch; a duplicate passenger email returns "Passenger must have a unique email address."
A public booking missing a single clear primary passenger, or whose primary passenger has no valid email, is rejected with a message naming the problem.
Assigning more passengers a real pickup location than the number who opted into transfer returns a message stating exactly how many were scheduled versus how many were selected.
Requesting the yacht search page without both a currency and a start date returns a message listing which required parameters are missing.
Reducing a booking's passenger count below the number already registered on it returns "Number of passengers must be greater than or equal to added passengers!"
Attempting to book a yacht that isn't available for the exact requested dates returns "Yacht is not available for the selected date range."

permissions.fact: Searching for yachts, viewing details, getting a cost preview, and submitting a booking on the public site are all open to anyone, without needing an account.
Creating, editing, and confirming a booking internally all require staff to be logged in and hold the relevant permission.

Automated background processes (cancelling overdue pending bookings, marking departed bookings, sending them to accounting, assigning crew) run on a system-level schedule rather than through a staff-operated screen.

field_meanings.fact: Number of Passengers / Number Who Took Transfer — how many people are traveling on the booking, and how many of them opted into the paid pickup/transfer service.
Sub Total / Discount / Grand Total / Due — the total price before any discount, the combined discount applied, the final payable total, and how much is still owed.
First Payment Deadline / Remaining Balance Deadline — the dates by which the deposit and the remaining balance are due, set from the charter provider's own payment schedule.
Manually Added Booking — a booking for a yacht entered by staff outside the normal provider catalog, which skips live availability checks and uses a staff-entered price instead of a calculated one.
Departed — marks a booking whose trip start date has passed, set automatically once that date arrives.

Booking Status (Pending, Booked, Cancelled) — a yacht booking starts Pending, becomes Booked once staff confirm the reservation with the charter provider, and becomes Cancelled if the reservation fails, the payment deadline passes, or it's cancelled outright.

journeys.fact: A customer searches available yachts by destination and date, views full details of one, adds passengers/extras/supplements, previews the full cost, and submits the booking themselves without needing to create an account first.

Behind the scenes, the booking is placed as pending, a reservation is opened with the actual charter provider, and confirmation emails go out to both the customer and staff; if the reservation can't be opened, the booking is automatically cancelled instead of being left incomplete.
Staff review a pending booking and explicitly confirm it, which locks in the reservation with the charter provider and marks the booking as booked.
Staff can also create or edit a booking directly, including for yachts added manually outside the usual provider catalog.
If a customer doesn't pay their deposit in time, the booking is automatically cancelled without staff needing to intervene.

side_effects.fact: Placing, confirming, updating, cancelling, and completing a yacht booking each notify the accounting system so the platform's financial records stay current.
A yacht booking uses the same underlying booking record as tour and hotel bookings, so it shows up alongside them wherever bookings are managed.
Booking creation and cancellation update any coupon's usage record if a coupon was applied.
Confirmation and update emails are sent automatically to the customer at the relevant points in the booking's lifecycle.
For crewed yachts, crew is automatically assigned to a booking shortly before departure without a separate staff action.

features.name: Supplements & Add-ons
features.summary: Optional add-on products/supplements with groups, categories and local pricing.

workflows.fact: Staff create a supplement (an optional add-on) with a name, description, price, pricing unit, and category; if no tax class is chosen, the system defaults it to "No VAT".
Creating or editing a supplement automatically creates or updates a translation of it in the tenant's default language, and generates a converted price for every active currency the tenant supports.
Staff organize supplements into categories, which can themselves be nested under a parent category.
Staff can override a supplement's automatically-converted price for one specific currency without touching its base price.
Staff add further translations of a supplement or category one language at a time; requesting a translation that doesn't exist yet returns an empty result rather than an error.
Staff can upload, replace, or delete a promotional image on a supplement.
Staff deactivate a supplement rather than deleting it outright — there's no delete action available for supplements or categories, only status toggling.
When a new currency is turned on for the tenant, every active supplement automatically gets a price generated in that currency.
A separate central-administration process (not a regular staff login) can manage the supplement catalog across all tenants.

rules.fact: A supplement category's name must be unique — a duplicate is rejected outright rather than merged or overwritten.
A supplement can only be priced in one of eight ways: once per booking, per day, per week, or per night, each either as a flat charge or multiplied by the number of passengers.
The default pricing basis for a new supplement is once per person per booking.
A supplement can be marked as not contributing to the total price even though it's still listed — useful for informational or already-included items.
If no tax class is set on a supplement, it defaults to "No VAT".
Only tags belonging to the supplement category can be attached to a supplement.
A converted price in a foreign currency is rounded to the nearest 5 units; a price shown in the tenant's own base currency is just rounded normally.
A supplement can't be deactivated while it's attached to any currently active booking, active tour, or active custom tour offer.
Supplements can be grouped so customers pick just one option from a set (like a meal choice) or several, and a group can be marked as requiring a selection.

validations.fact: Creating a supplement category with a name that already exists returns "{Category} with this name already exists."
Requesting a translation without specifying which language returns "Language code is required".
Adding a translation in an inactive language returns "Language is not valid."
Requesting or setting a price in a currency that isn't recognized returns "currency not found".
