Trying to deactivate a supplement still in use by an active booking, tour, or custom tour offer returns "This supplement is used in active tour, booking or custom tour."
Uploaded images are checked for file size and image type; invalid ones are rejected.

permissions.fact: Creating, editing, categorizing, pricing, and translating supplements all require staff to be logged in and hold the corresponding permission.
Uploading or deleting a supplement image only requires being logged in.
Managing the supplement catalog from the platform's central administration console uses a separate system-level authorization, not a normal staff login.

field_meanings.fact: Name / Description — the display name and detail text for the add-on.
Price — the supplement's base price in the tenant's own currency, from which all other currency prices are derived.
Pricing Unit — how the supplement is charged: once per booking, per day, per week, or per night, each either flat or multiplied by passenger count.
Mandatory — whether the supplement must always be included wherever it's offered, with no option to remove it.
Contributes to Total — whether the supplement's price is counted in the overall total, even when it's still shown to the customer.
Complimentary — marks the supplement as free of charge.
Sales Cut-Off — an optional rule limiting how close to departure the supplement can still be sold.
Category — the catalog grouping this supplement belongs to, which can itself sit under a parent category.
Supplier — the external supplier who provides or fulfills this add-on, if any.
Tax Class — the tax rule applied to this supplement's price; defaults to "No VAT" if not set.
Supplement Group (Single/Multiple Choice, Required) — a cluster of related supplements presented together, either as a single choice or multiple choices, optionally required.
Translation (Name, Description) — the supplement's or category's content shown to customers in a specific language.

journeys.fact: To add a new add-on: staff enter its name, price, pricing unit, and category; the system fills in a default-language translation and prices in every supported currency automatically, without extra steps.
To organize the catalog: staff set up categories (optionally nested) before assigning supplements to them; a duplicate category name is rejected immediately.
To adjust pricing for a specific market: staff override the auto-converted price for one currency directly, without changing the supplement's base price.
To make a supplement available in more languages: staff add one translation per language; a language that isn't active can't be used for a translation.
To retire a supplement: staff deactivate it, which is blocked while it's still attached to any active booking, tour, or custom tour offer — those need to be resolved first.

side_effects.fact: A supplement's catalog entry is shared across features — it's referenced from Tours, Bookings, and Custom Tour Offers, which is exactly why deactivating an in-use supplement is blocked.
Turning on a new currency for the tenant automatically prices every active supplement in that currency.
A supplement's price calculation (for a given trip's dates and passenger count) is shared logic other features draw on when attaching a supplement to a booking.

features.name: Products
features.summary: Generic sellable products with categories, images, files and notes.

workflows.fact: Staff create a product with its name, supplier(s), location/address, and contact details.
Creating a product automatically creates a matching translation in the tenant's default language.
Staff organize a product into categories, each scoped to that one product rather than shared across the whole catalog.
Staff upload a gallery of images to a product, optionally marking one as the primary image, and add alt text for accessibility.
Staff upload a single representative image to a category.
Staff attach documents (contracts, spec sheets, etc.) to a product, giving each one a display name.
Staff add free-text internal notes to a product, shown newest first, each attributed to the staff member who wrote it.
Staff add translations of a product or category one language at a time.
Editing a product's name while working in a specific language updates that language's translation, not the original default-language name.
Staff deactivate a product or category as a separate action from editing its content.

rules.fact: A product or category can only have one translation per language — a duplicate is rejected.
Every new product and category automatically gets a translation created in the tenant's default language, with no separate step required.
A translation can only be added in a language that's currently active.
Attached files must be under 10 MB and one of a limited set of file types (images, PDF, plain text, Word documents).
A product's active/inactive status can only be changed through its dedicated status action, not through the general edit form.
Searching the product or category list matches either the base name or its translated name in whichever language is being viewed.

validations.fact: Changing a product's or category's status without specifying active/inactive returns "'is_active' field is required."
Adding a translation in an inactive language returns "Language is not active."
Adding a second translation for a language that already has one returns "A multilanguage entry for this product and language already exists." (or the equivalent for a category).
Requesting a product's translation without specifying which language returns "language_code query parameter or Accept-Language header is required."
Uploading a file of an unsupported type is rejected, naming which file types are actually allowed.
Uploading a file over 10 MB is rejected.
Attaching a file without giving it a name is rejected — a name is required alongside the file.

permissions.fact: Creating, editing, categorizing, uploading images/files, adding notes, and translating products all require staff to be logged in and hold the corresponding permission.

field_meanings.fact: Name / Description / Remarks — the product's display name, customer-facing description, and internal notes text (Remarks is separate from the internal Notes list).
Supplier Type / Supplier — the kind of vendor this product comes from, and the actual vendor(s) fulfilling it; a product can be linked to more than one supplier.
Contact Person Name / Email — the point of contact at the supplier or location for this product.
Location, Territory, Address — where the product is physically located or delivered from.
Map URL — a link to an external map pinpointing the product's location.
Image / Primary Image — a picture in the product's gallery, with one optionally marked as the main image.
File / File Name — a downloadable document attached to the product, such as a contract or spec sheet.
Note — a free-text internal comment about the product, visible only to staff.
Category — a grouping under one specific product, used to organize what's sellable under it; each category belongs to exactly one product.
Active/Inactive — whether the product or category is currently published, toggled only through its dedicated status action.

journeys.fact: To list a new product: staff enter its name, supplier(s), location, and contact details; a translation in the tenant's default language is created automatically.
To organize it: staff add categories scoped to that product, each with its own name, description, and image.
To flesh it out: staff upload a gallery of images (with one as the main image), attach relevant documents, and leave internal notes for other staff.
To support more markets: staff add a translation per additional language needed.
To take it offline: staff deactivate it as a distinct action from editing its content.

side_effects.fact: A product exists purely as a standalone catalog/directory entry — it does not attach to bookings, tours, hotels, yacht charters, or custom tour offers, and has no pricing or tax configuration of its own.

features.name: Pricing & Price Manager
features.summary: Pricing projects, price calculation, pricing webhooks and logs across products.

workflows.fact: An external pricing engine (Beetroot) sends a webhook when a pricing project becomes active or when next week's price schedule is ready; the system records the event and, for those two event types, immediately asks the scheduler to fetch fresh price recommendations for that project's tours.
The scheduled sync fetches the pricing project's tour list and a price recommendation per tour from the external engine, then creates one pending pricing log per tour holding the suggested price.
A suggested price is rounded up to the nearest 50 (currency units) before being stored as the tour's new standard price on the log.

Staff can list pending pricing logs, then apply one or many to actually update the tour's price, or reject them instead; either action requires the log's price to actually differ from the tour's current price and the tour to not have already departed.
If the tenant has automatic price synchronization turned on, a scheduled job applies pending logs on their own without staff review, but only for logs created the same week as today's automatic run.

Applying a log updates the tour's standard price and recalculates the tour's dependent fees (booking fee, cancellation fee, second-payment amount, travel-insurance fee) to match the new price, subject to the tour's existing minimum/maximum price limits.
Staff can add a note when applying or rejecting a log, and can view a tour's full pricing history (applied and rejected logs) separately from the pending queue.

rules.fact: A suggested price is always rounded up to the nearest 50.

A pricing log only counts as actionable (pending, applicable) if its new price differs from the tour's price at the time, the log's pricing project is currently active (today falls within the project's start/end date), and the tour has not departed.
Automatic (unattended) apply additionally requires the log to have been created in the same scheduling run as today's automatic sync — older pending logs are left for manual review.
Automatic apply only runs at all if the tenant's automatic price synchronization setting is switched on; otherwise staff must apply or reject every log by hand.
A tour's price change from this feature still has to respect the tour's own minimum/maximum standard price limits, same as a manual price edit.

validations.fact: Applying or rejecting logs when none are applicable returns a success response saying no applicable pricing logs were found, rather than an error.

If some (but not all) selected logs fail to apply, staff still get the successfully applied ones plus a message stating how many applied vs. how many could not be, asking them to contact an administrator for the rest.
Only logs linked to a Tour can be applied through this workflow today; a log linked to any other record type is reported back as unsupported.

permissions.fact: Viewing, applying, and rejecting pricing logs requires the standard staff model permissions for pricing logs plus the tenant having the dynamic-pricing add-on enabled on its subscription plan.

The webhook that receives events from the external pricing engine, and the scheduled automatic-apply job, authenticate as the system itself (not as a staff user) — they are machine-to-machine endpoints, not something a staff member calls directly.

field_meanings.fact: A pricing log's status is Pending (awaiting a decision), Accepted (applied to the tour), Rejected (a staff member declined it), or Failed (the sync itself did not complete).
A pricing project is the external engine's grouping of tours that share one pricing run, with its own active date range and tour list; a project only feeds price recommendations while it is active.

journeys.fact: Staff open the pending pricing queue, see each tour's current price next to the newly suggested one, and either apply the suggestion (optionally with a note) or reject it (optionally with a note) — nothing changes on the tour until one of those actions happens, unless automatic sync is on.
Staff can look at a single tour's own pricing history to see every past applied or rejected suggestion for that tour, separate from the tenant-wide pending queue.

side_effects.fact: Applying a pricing log changes the tour's price and its dependent fees, which is the same tour data the Tours feature validates and displays elsewhere.

features.name: Payments
features.summary: Payment methods, transactions, settlements, OCR payment import, and provider integrations (AltaPay).

workflows.fact: A payment can be applied to a booking, a ResPay account, an invoice, or a gift card — each routed to its own handler, but all recorded as a Transaction.
A successful booking payment updates the booking's paid amount, cancels any pending payment-reminder emails for it, and finalizes the booking if it was still a draft.
Once a booking payment is processed, it can be pushed to the tenant's connected accounting system if that hasn't happened yet.

A refund creates its own transaction record (using a dedicated refund payment method) rather than reversing the original payment record, and reduces the booking's recorded paid amount by the refunded amount.
Staff can record a manual payment directly (e.g. bank transfer, cash) as an admin-only action, separate from the automated provider payment flows.

rules.fact: A refund can't be processed through a payment method that isn't configured for the tenant — except when the refund is being triggered automatically as part of cancelling a booking, which is allowed regardless.

Every transaction tracks both a payment status (pending/success/failed) and a separate settlement status, since a payment succeeding and that payment being settled/reconciled with accounting are tracked as two different states.

validations.fact: Attempting a refund through an unconfigured payment method is rejected with 'Payment Method is not configured.' (except for cancellation-triggered refunds).

permissions.fact: Viewing/managing transactions requires staff authentication plus Django model permissions.
Recording a manual payment is restricted to admin users specifically, not just any authenticated staff member.
A passenger can view their own transaction history (or, for staff impersonating a passenger, a read-only view of it); public payment status lookup requires no authentication at all.
Public-facing payment status information requires no authentication.

field_meanings.fact: A Transaction's amount is what the transaction covers; pending_amount tracks how much of it is still awaiting completion (relevant for payment methods that don't settle instantly).
A transaction can be linked to a booking, a ResPay account, a billing invoice, or a gift card — which one it's linked to determines what business impact processing it has.

journeys.fact: A customer pays for their booking online through one of the tenant's supported payment options; on success, the booking's balance updates immediately and any pending payment reminder for it is cancelled.
When a booking is cancelled, any refund owed is created and processed automatically as part of the cancellation, without a separate manual refund step.

side_effects.fact: Payments and refunds both interact with the tenant's connected accounting system, marking a transaction as sent once that sync succeeds.

features.name: ResPay Payments
features.summary: ResPay payment provider integration and its configuration.

workflows.fact: Staff create a standalone payment request (not tied to a booking): an amount, currency, due date, and the customer's email, choosing whether to notify the customer by email, SMS, or both.

Creating the request generates a unique payment code and a payment link, and — if requested — immediately sends the customer an email containing that link; a reminder is also scheduled ahead of the due date.

The customer opens the payment link's public page, which shows the company's name and logo, the amount and due date, and the payment methods available to pay with (manual, refund, and invoice payment are never offered here).

The customer completes payment through one of the offered payment providers (Klarna, Trustly, or Altapay); once the provider confirms the payment, the request's status becomes Paid and an internal confirmation email is sent to whoever created the request.
Staff can manually resend a reminder to the customer at any time before the request is paid.
Staff can cancel a request that has not yet been paid or expired.
Once a request is paid, staff can mark it as accounted (recorded in accounting) and see who marked it and when; a request cannot be marked accounted while still pending, expired, failed, or canceled.
A scheduled job automatically marks any pending request whose due date has passed as Expired.
A day before a pending request's due date, a scheduled job emails the staff member who created it, listing every customer whose payment link is about to expire.
Staff can export all payment requests to an Excel report, and view a dashboard summary comparing this month's paid and outstanding totals to last month's.

rules.fact: A payment request can only be created if the tenant has an active Resemolnet payment provider connection configured; otherwise creation is rejected.
A request already Paid or Expired cannot be canceled.
Only a Paid request can be marked accounted; Pending, Expired, Failed, or Canceled requests are rejected.
A reminder cannot be sent for a request that has already been paid.

A request's public payment page and payment link stop working once the request is no longer active, has passed its due date, or has already been paid — the customer sees a not-found/expired message instead.

Whether payment requests automatically email or SMS customers, whether internal staff get expiry/paid-reminder notifications, and how long a link stays valid before expiring (and how long before that an internal expiry warning goes out) are all set per tenant in the feature's configuration.

validations.fact: The public payment page and the customer-facing payment status both treat a request as Expired the moment its due date passes, even before the scheduled cleanup job has run, so a customer can never pay a link past its due date.
Payment codes are always unique, so a payment link can never be shared by more than one request.

permissions.fact: Any authenticated staff member can create and list payment requests; canceling, marking accounted, and retrieving a single request's detail additionally require the standard staff model permissions.

The public payment page and the customer's checkout endpoints (Klarna, Trustly, Altapay) need no staff login at all — they identify the request purely by its unique payment code, so anyone with the link's code can view and pay it.
The scheduled expiry and internal-reminder jobs run as the system itself via a machine API key, not as a staff user.

field_meanings.fact: A payment request's status is Pending (link sent, awaiting payment), Paid (successfully paid), Expired (due date passed without payment), Failed (a payment attempt did not go through), or Canceled (a staff member canceled it).
"Accounted" marks that a paid request has been recorded for accounting purposes, separate from its payment status, with who accounted it and when.
"Sent by" records whether the payment link was delivered to the customer by email, SMS, or both.

journeys.fact: A staff member creates a payment request for a customer (e.g. for a charge outside a normal booking flow), the customer receives the link by email and/or SMS, opens it, picks a payment method, and pays; the staff member is notified by email once it's paid, and can later mark it as accounted.

If a customer hasn't paid yet, they may get an automatic or staff-sent reminder before the link expires; if the due date passes unpaid, the link stops working and the staff member who created it is warned in advance.

side_effects.fact: A completed ResPay payment creates a Transaction record, the same record type the Payments feature uses for booking payments, linking this payment request to that shared transaction history.

features.name: Billing & Invoicing
features.summary: Billing lines and account invoices generated from bookings.

workflows.fact: A booking's charges (tour price, supplements, extras, fees) accumulate as Billing Lines, which get grouped onto an Account Invoice for that booking.

An invoice starts as a Draft and is editable in that state; issuing it locks it (no longer editable), assigns it a permanent invoice number and a payment reference number, and — if the tenant has accounting integration enabled — sends it there.
Issuing an invoice for a booking still in Quote status automatically accepts that quote as part of the same step.

An issued invoice can be voided (unlinking its billing lines and marking it void) or credited (generating a credit note that reverses its billing lines) — both only apply to invoices that are actually in Issued status.
Voiding an invoice that's already been booked in the connected accounting system is blocked, since undoing it there isn't possible from this side.

rules.fact: An invoice cannot be issued twice — issuing an already-issued invoice is rejected outright.
An invoice with no billing lines cannot be issued.
An invoice can only be voided if it's currently Issued, and only if it hasn't been paid or partially paid — a paid invoice must be credited, not voided.
An invoice can only be credited if it's currently Issued.
Every billing line carries its own VAT percentage and VAT amount, calculated per line rather than once for the whole invoice.

validations.fact: Issuing an already-issued invoice is rejected with 'Cannot issue an already issued invoice.'
Issuing an invoice with no billing lines is rejected with 'Cannot issue an invoice with no billing lines.'
Voiding a non-issued invoice is rejected with 'Cannot void a non-issued invoice.'; voiding a paid or partially-paid one is rejected with 'Cannot void a paid invoice.'
Voiding an invoice already booked in the connected accounting system is rejected with 'Cannot void an invoice that is already booked in the accounting service.'
Crediting a non-issued invoice is rejected with 'This invoice cannot be credited as it is not issued.'

permissions.fact: All invoice and billing-line operations (view, create, issue, void, credit, delete, download, email) require staff authentication.

field_meanings.fact: An invoice's status (Draft, Issued, Void) is separate from its payment status (Unpaid, Partially Paid, Paid) — an invoice can be Issued and still Unpaid, or Issued and fully Paid.

A billing line can belong to more than one kind of source (a booking's tour price, a supplement, an extra, a supplier charge) via a generic content-type link, letting one invoice combine charges from different parts of a booking.
An invoice is only editable while it's in Draft status — once issued, its content is locked.

journeys.fact: Staff review a booking's accumulated billing lines, generate a draft invoice, and issue it once it's correct — issuing locks the invoice, generates its final numbering, and (if enabled) pushes it to the connected accounting system.
If an issued invoice turns out to be wrong before any payment, staff void it; if it's already been paid, staff issue a credit note against it instead.

side_effects.fact: Issuing an invoice updates every billing line on it to reflect that it's now part of an issued invoice, and can trigger sending the invoice to the tenant's connected accounting system.
Voiding an invoice snapshots its billing lines onto the invoice record itself before unlinking them, preserving a record of what the invoice contained.

features.name: Coupons
features.summary: Discount coupons with local pricing and usage tracking.

workflows.fact: Staff create a coupon with a unique code, a discount (either a percentage or a fixed amount), a validity date range, how many times it can be used in total, and whether it applies to all tours or only specific tours they pick.

A fixed-amount coupon's discount is automatically converted into every active currency the tenant supports, so the same coupon shows a locally appropriate discount no matter which currency a customer is browsing in.
Before checkout, a customer (or the booking preview) can check whether a coupon code is valid for a specific tour, and see the discount amount and type it would apply.

When a booking is completed with a coupon code attached, the coupon's usage count goes up by one and the booking is recorded against that coupon; if the booking is later cancelled, the usage count goes back down and the record is removed.
A coupon automatically turns itself off once its usage count reaches its use limit, and turns back on if usage drops back below the limit (for example after a cancellation).
Staff can view every booking that has used a specific coupon, filterable by booking reference, status, and date.
Staff can turn a coupon on or off directly, and can list which tours a coupon is currently valid for.

rules.fact: A coupon's discount can never be set to 0 — creating or updating one with a zero discount is rejected.
A coupon applies either to every tour ("all tour") or to a specific list of tours the staff member picks — not a mix decided per booking.
A coupon's valid-to date always covers the entire last day (through 23:59:59), so a coupon set to expire on a given date is still usable any time that day.
Once a coupon has been used at least once, its code, discount, and discount type can no longer be edited — only its validity dates, use limit, tours, description, and active status can still change.
A coupon's active status cannot be changed by hand once its use limit has been reached — the system reports that the limit has been exceeded.
A use limit of 0 means the coupon can be used an unlimited number of times and never auto-deactivates from usage.
For a fixed-amount coupon, the discount applied on a booking never exceeds the booking's own cost — a coupon can bring a booking to zero but never below it.
A coupon only validates successfully if it is currently active and today falls within its validity date range; an expired, not-yet-active, or inactive coupon is treated as invalid.

validations.fact: Checking a coupon against a tour that doesn't exist or is inactive is rejected as an invalid tour, rather than as an invalid coupon.
Applying an unknown coupon code to a booking, or one that is inactive or has exceeded its usage limit, is rejected outright rather than silently ignored.

permissions.fact: Creating, updating, listing, retrieving, activating/deactivating a coupon, and viewing which bookings used it all require standard staff model permissions.
Checking whether a coupon code is valid for a tour is a public action — no staff login is required, since customers use it while browsing a tour.

field_meanings.fact: "Use limit" is the total number of bookings a coupon can be used on across all customers combined, not a per-customer limit; 0 means unlimited.
"Used count" tracks how many times a coupon has actually been applied to a completed booking so far.
Discount type is either "Percentage" (a percent off the booking cost) or "Amount" (a fixed sum off, converted per currency).
Coupon type is either "All Tour" (usable on any tour) or "Specific Tour" (only usable on the tours explicitly attached to the coupon).

journeys.fact: A customer enters a coupon code while browsing or booking a tour; the system tells them immediately whether it's valid for that tour and what discount it gives, before they commit to the booking.
Once the booking with that coupon is confirmed, the discount is applied and the coupon's usage count increases; if the customer later cancels the booking, the coupon's usage count is given back.

side_effects.fact: Applying a coupon to a booking reduces the price the Bookings feature charges for that booking, and a cancellation there reverses the coupon's usage count here.

features.name: Gift Cards
features.summary: Gift cards with configurable greeting texts, images and usage history.

workflows.fact: A gift card can be created two ways: staff create an internal gift card directly from the admin (active immediately, no separate payment step), or a customer buys one through a public purchase flow that starts the card as Inactive and only activates it once payment succeeds.

Creating a gift card records the recipient's name and email, the amount, an expiry date, an optional personal note, a greeting text, and an optional image; if requested, the card is emailed to the recipient as a PDF attachment right away.
A publicly purchased gift card's expiry date is always set automatically from the tenant's configured number of expiry days from the purchase date — the customer cannot choose it.
Once a purchased gift card's payment completes through the payment provider, the card automatically becomes Active and is marked paid, and the customer can then start spending it.

Staff maintain a reusable library of greeting texts (with translations) and a gallery of images that customers and staff pick from when creating a card, instead of writing free text or uploading a new image each time.

A staff member or, through the passenger portal, the customer can apply a gift card to an existing booking's outstanding balance, spending part or all of the card's remaining amount against what's still due.

Applying a gift card creates a payment record against the booking and, if that clears the full amount due, marks the booking as paid; it also records the gift card usage against that specific booking so there's a history of where each card's balance went.
Staff can look up a gift card's remaining balance and whether it's currently valid by its code, either from the admin or from the customer-facing passenger portal.
Staff can view a summary of gift card sales and how much unspent value is still outstanding across a chosen date range.

rules.fact: A gift card can only be spent on bookings priced in SEK — it cannot be applied to a booking in any other currency.

The amount applied from a gift card to a booking is capped at whichever is smallest: the amount requested, the card's remaining balance, or the booking's outstanding due amount — it can never exceed any of those.
A gift card cannot be applied to a booking that has already been fully paid, and cannot be applied for zero or a negative amount.

A gift card only counts as valid to redeem if it is Active, still marked usable, and has not passed its expiry date; an inactive, wrong-status, or expired card is rejected with the specific reason why.
Once a gift card is no longer a Draft, most of its details (recipient, amount, code) can no longer be changed — only its expiry date, note, image, and greeting text remain editable.

A scheduled job automatically expires any gift card past its expiry date and deactivates it; a paid card that still had unspent balance when it expired is recorded for accounting so that unused value isn't lost from the books.
A Draft gift card that sits unpurchased/unfinished past the tenant's configured number of days is automatically deleted, along with any image uploaded just for it.

validations.fact: Looking up a gift card's remaining amount or validity by a code that doesn't exist is rejected as not found, with the specific invalid reason (not active, wrong status, expired) surfaced when applying it to a booking.

permissions.fact: Creating, updating, listing, viewing summaries, updating status, and downloading a gift card as PDF from the admin all require an authenticated staff user (several also require standard staff model permissions).

Buying a gift card publicly needs no login; checking a card's remaining balance or applying it through the passenger portal is restricted to that customer's own impersonated session, not open to anyone.
The scheduled expiry and draft-cleanup jobs run as the system itself via a machine API key, not as a staff action.

field_meanings.fact: A gift card's status is Draft (being set up, not yet purchased/finalized), Active (usable), Inactive (turned off), Expired (past its expiry date), or reflects how much of it has been used (Unused, Partially Used, Used).
"Remaining amount" is the card's total value minus what's already been spent — the balance still available to redeem.
"Internal gift card" marks a card staff issued directly (for example, as a goodwill gesture) rather than one a customer purchased; it skips the payment step and is active right away.

journeys.fact: A customer buys a gift card for someone through the public purchase flow, picking a greeting text, image, amount, and the recipient's details, then pays; once payment succeeds the card becomes active and (if chosen) the recipient gets it by email as a PDF.

A recipient later books a tour and enters their gift card code, or asks staff to apply it, to cover some or all of what they owe; the booking's remaining due amount drops by the amount used, and the card's own remaining balance drops to match.

side_effects.fact: Applying a gift card to a booking creates the same kind of payment transaction record used for other booking payments, and can mark the booking as fully paid.

features.name: Rewards & Loyalty
features.summary: Loyalty point accounts, reward tiers, and a point ledger.

workflows.fact: No workflow exists yet: reward/ contains only three models (RewardTier, RewardPointAccount, RewardPointLedgerEntry) with no services, views, or urls.py, and nothing outside the app references them.

field_meanings.fact: The data model anticipates a tiered points program: a RewardTier defines an earn rate and point money-value; a RewardPointAccount ties one passenger to one tier; a RewardPointLedgerEntry records signed point credits/debits (earn, redeem, cancellation re-credit, manual credit/debit, backfill, share debit/credit, expiry) with tier/rate snapshots.

features.name: VAT & Tax Classes
features.summary: VAT classes, VAT/cost accounts and tax categorisation used in billing.

workflows.fact: Staff create VAT classes — a name, a tax percentage, whether it should appear on invoices, and which VAT type(s) it belongs to — for use when pricing tours, supplements, and other sellable items.
Staff separately maintain VAT types (broad tax categories a VAT class can belong to) and a set of VAT accounts and cost accounts, which connect VAT classes to the tenant's accounting setup.
Staff can turn a VAT class, VAT account, or cost account on or off, and browse VAT classes filtered by VAT type.

rules.fact: A VAT type can only have one VAT class at any given tax percentage — creating or editing a class into a percentage that's already used by another class of the same type is rejected.
The built-in "No VAT" class's name and tax percentage can never be changed, and its active/inactive status can never be changed either — it's a fixed, permanent option.

A VAT class currently selected on any active tour or active supplement cannot have its status changed — it must first be removed from every active tour and supplement before it can be deactivated (or reactivated).
A VAT class's tax percentage must be between 0 and 100.

validations.fact: Every VAT class name must be unique across the tenant.

permissions.fact: Creating, editing, listing, and changing the status of VAT classes, VAT types, VAT accounts, and cost accounts all require an authenticated staff user with the standard staff model permissions — there is no customer-facing access to any of this.

field_meanings.fact: A VAT class's tax percentage is the rate charged on whatever it's attached to (a tour, a supplement, and so on).
"Will show in invoice" controls whether this VAT class's tax line is visible on the customer-facing invoice, separate from whether the tax itself is applied.
A VAT type is a broader tax category (for example, standard vs. reduced rate) that groups related VAT classes together, and is what the one-class-per-percentage rule is scoped to.
VAT accounts and cost accounts are named references into the tenant's accounting setup, linked to a VAT class so its tax gets recorded to the right place in the books.

journeys.fact: Staff set up the tenant's tax categories once (VAT types, VAT classes with their percentages, and the accounting accounts they post to), then simply pick the right VAT class when pricing a tour or supplement elsewhere — customers never interact with VAT classes directly.

side_effects.fact: The VAT class picked on a tour or supplement determines the tax rate billing calculates and shows for that item; this feature only defines the rates and accounting targets, not how they're applied to a specific sale.

features.name: Accounting Integration
features.summary: Integration with external accounting providers: projects, VAT codes, customers, cost centers, event sync.

workflows.fact: The tenant connects to one external accounting/bookkeeping system at a time (Fortnox or PowerOffice); once connected, the platform automatically records business events there as accounting vouchers and keeps a log of every attempt.

features.name: Suppliers
features.summary: Suppliers, supplier types, supplier invoices and their financial/VAT accounts.

workflows.fact: Staff maintain a directory of suppliers (transport, flight, accommodation, and other vendors) with contact, financial, and accounting defaults, grouped by supplier type; a supplier's own system can also be given a company-level API token to fetch its own invoices and register the costs it's billed for.

features.name: Tour Guides
features.summary: Tour guides, guide types and their time-slot availability.

workflows.fact: Staff set up guide types (categories like driver-guide or local guide) before guides can be categorized.
Staff create a tour guide with personal, contact, and document details; this automatically creates or links a login account and profile for that guide.
A guide can sign in and view/edit their own profile, including uploading their contract, flight ticket, and photo.
Staff (or the guide) define time-slot windows stating when the guide is available to be assigned to tours.
When building a tour, staff look up which guides of a given type are available for the tour's exact dates.
Staff assign an available guide to a tour, optionally also linking them to one of the tour's vehicles.
Staff can remove a guide from a tour, which frees up their availability again and detaches any vehicle link.
Staff can view a consolidated board of every tour's guide assignments grouped by guide type and vehicle, or drill into one guide's full assignment list.
Staff download a passenger manifest for a tour or a specific vehicle on it, listing every traveling passenger's contact, passport, pickup, and allergy details for the assigned guide to use.
Staff deactivate a guide when they're no longer available, which also deactivates their login unless they hold an admin role.

rules.fact: A guide's availability window must be at least 5 days long, can't start in the past, and its start date can't come after its end date.
A guide's available time-slot windows can't overlap each other.
A guide's availability window can't be shrunk to cut out a tour already assigned within it.
Each guide's email must be unique, and each guide-type label must be unique.
Only one guide of a given type can be assigned to a specific vehicle on a tour, and a guide can only be linked to one vehicle per tour.
A guide can only be assigned to a tour if they have an availability window that fully covers the tour's departure-to-return dates.
Guides can't be assigned to or removed from a tour once its return date has already passed.
A guide can't be deactivated while they're still assigned to any active tour.
An availability window can't be deactivated or removed while it has an active tour attached to it.

validations.fact: Setting an availability window's start date before today returns "Start date can not be less than today."
Setting a start date after the end date returns "Start date can not be greater than end date."
Setting a window shorter than 5 days returns "The duration cannot be less than 5 days."
Creating an availability window that overlaps another one returns "This timeslot overlap with another timeslot."
Shrinking a window to exclude an already-assigned tour returns "This time range has active tour."
Trying to deactivate a window still assigned to a tour returns "This time slot is assigned to tour".
Trying to remove a window still assigned to a tour returns a message naming which active tour(s) are blocking it.
Trying to deactivate a guide still assigned to an active tour returns "This tour guide has active tour."
Trying to assign a guide with no availability covering the tour's dates returns "Available time slot not found for this tour guide."
Picking a vehicle that isn't part of the tour being assigned returns a message naming the mismatch.
Assigning a second guide of the same type to a vehicle that already has one returns a message naming the conflict.
Assigning a guide who already has a different vehicle on the same tour returns a message naming the conflict.
Assigning or removing a guide on a tour whose return date has passed returns a message naming the tour and stating the return date has passed.
Downloading a passenger manifest for a tour with no traveling passengers returns "No passengers found for this tour."

permissions.fact: Creating, editing, and deactivating guides and guide types requires staff to be logged in and hold the corresponding permission.
A guide can view and edit their own profile once logged in.
Viewing available guides, assigning a guide to a tour, and removing a guide from a tour only require being logged in, without a specific permission check.
Only the guide who owns a time-slot window can view, edit, or change the status of it themselves.
Viewing the consolidated guide-assignment board and managing availability windows requires staff to be logged in and hold the corresponding permission.

field_meanings.fact: Guide Type — the category of guide (e.g. driver-guide, local guide), configured by staff and used both to find available guides and to enforce one-guide-per-type-per-vehicle.
Name, Position, Employee ID — the guide's identifying and role details.
License / License Number — the guide's professional license type and number.
Home Base — the guide's home station or location they're normally based out of.
Contract File, Flight Ticket File, Profile Picture — documents and photo uploaded for the guide.
Passport / Personal ID details, Allergy info, Emergency Contact — the guide's travel and safety details, mirrored into their linked profile.
Feedback — free-text notes recording feedback about the guide's performance.
Active/Inactive — whether the guide is currently employable and assignable; a guide can't be deactivated while still assigned to an active tour.
Availability Window (Start Date, End Date) — the date range during which a guide has said they're available to be assigned to a tour.
Available — whether an availability window is currently open for new assignment; it's automatically closed alongside deactivating the window itself.
Assigned Tours (on a window) — which tour(s) have actually been booked into a given availability window.

journeys.fact: To onboard a guide: staff first make sure the relevant guide type exists, then create the guide's record with their personal and contact details; the guide immediately gets a login they can use to manage their own profile.
To set up availability: staff or the guide themselves add windows of dates the guide is free to be assigned, each at least 5 days long and never overlapping another window.
To staff a tour: staff search for guides of the needed type who are available for the tour's exact dates, then assign one — optionally also linking them to a specific vehicle on that tour.
To review coverage: staff open a board showing every tour's guide assignments by type and vehicle, or look at one guide's full workload across tours.
To prepare a guide for departure: staff download a passenger manifest for the tour or a specific vehicle, listing every traveler's contact, passport, pickup, and allergy details.
To retire a guide: staff deactivate them, which is blocked while they're still assigned to an active tour, and which also disables their login unless they hold an admin role.

side_effects.fact: Creating a guide creates or updates a linked login account and profile, giving the guide portal access without a separate account-creation step.
Assigning a guide to a tour updates the guide's own tour list, their availability window's assigned-tours list, and — if a vehicle was chosen — the tour's vehicle roster, all together in one action.
Removing a guide from a tour reverses all of those links at once.
Deactivating an availability window automatically marks it as unavailable too.
The passenger manifest download draws on booking and ticketing data to assemble each traveler's full details for the guide.

features.name: Vehicles, Carriers & Stations
features.summary: Transport logistics: vehicles and types, home bases, carriers and pickup/drop stations.

workflows.fact: Staff create/edit vehicle types, home bases, and vehicles for use on tours.
A vehicle assigned to an active, not-yet-departed tour cannot be deactivated.
Staff create/edit stations and view station types for use as ticket departure/destination points.
A station can only be edited if both its current type and the new type are "Other"; otherwise the change is rejected.
A station cannot be deactivated unless its type is "Other", and not at all if it's currently used as a ticket's departure or destination station.
Creating or editing a station is rejected if another station with the same name and type already exists.
Carriers arrive automatically from a central sync feed matched by a unique signature key; an existing carrier is updated, a new one is created.
Staff can view carriers and edit a carrier's name directly; IATA/ICAO codes and active status stay under sync control.
Stations and station types can be synced in bulk from a central source, matched by a central record id.

rules.fact: A vehicle's IATA-style external reference id, if set, must be unique across all vehicles.
A carrier's IATA code is at most 2 characters and unique; its ICAO code, if set, is at most 4 characters and unique.
A carrier's signature key is unique and is what the sync feed uses to recognize the same carrier on repeat syncs.
On carrier sync, only the IATA code, ICAO code, and active status are updated on an existing match — the carrier's name is never overwritten by sync.
"Other" is the station type reserved for stations staff create themselves, as opposed to system-managed stations synced from a central source.
New stations created by staff are always assigned the "Other" type automatically.
Two stations are considered duplicates when they share both the same name and the same station type.
Vehicles, vehicle types, home bases, stations, and station types are never deleted through these screens, only deactivated.

validations.fact: A vehicle type's name must be unique.
A station type's name must be unique.
Deactivating a vehicle that's assigned to an active, not-departed tour is rejected with a message that the vehicle has an active tour assignment.
Editing a station whose current or new type isn't "Other" is rejected, telling staff to contact the BookingSystem admin instead.
Deactivating a station that isn't type "Other", or one currently set as a ticket's departure or destination station, is rejected.
Creating or editing a station that would duplicate an existing station's name and type is rejected with "Same station exists."

permissions.fact: Staff need the standard add/change/view model permissions to manage vehicles, vehicle types, home bases, stations, and station types; unauthenticated access is rejected.
Central sync of carriers, stations, and station types is performed by an automated system integration authenticated with an API key, not by a staff user.
Staff can view carriers and update a carrier's name, gated by standard model permissions.

field_meanings.fact: Vehicle Home Base is the depot/location a vehicle operates out of: a name, city, country, address, and optional map coordinates.
A vehicle's capacity is its total seat count, used to work out how many seats remain free once passengers are assigned.
A vehicle's external id is an optional reference code linking it to a record in another system.
A carrier's signature key is a one-time-generated key identifying the carrier for automated syncing, not a user-facing field.
A station's code is its short reference code (e.g. an airport code); its central id links it to the corresponding record in the central sync source.

journeys.fact: Staff set up vehicle types and home bases first, then create vehicles referencing them, so vehicles are ready to assign to tours and tour types.
Staff create custom ("Other"-type) stations for local pickup/drop points that aren't part of the synced airport list, then use them the same way as any other station.
Carriers mostly appear automatically as flights get synced; staff occasionally correct a carrier's display name without touching the codes that came from the sync.

side_effects.fact: Vehicles are assigned to tours and tour types, which track their own seat capacity and passenger counts separately from the vehicle's own capacity.
Stations are used as the departure and destination points on flight tickets.
Carriers are referenced on flight PNRs/tickets to identify which airline a segment is with.

features.name: Notifications (Email)
features.summary: Email events, templates, scheduled mail, recipients and delivery logs.

workflows.fact: Staff define email events — a name, subject, and content template, with a set of allowed placeholders (dynamic values) that content can reference — and connect them to a specific template on the tenant's connected email provider.

Staff can write a translated version of an event's subject/content per language; if they don't, the system automatically machine-translates the default-language content into every other active language, without ever overwriting a translation a staff member already wrote.
Staff connect one active email provider (currently Sendgrid) with its sender name and credentials; the platform sends every notification through that connection.

Business events elsewhere in the platform (a booking confirmation, a payment reminder, a flight ticket update, and so on) trigger an email event immediately, filling in its dynamic values with real data and rendering it in the recipient's preferred language.

Some notifications are scheduled ahead of time instead of sent immediately — tied to a specific record (like a booking) with a send date — either on a fixed daily batch, or, for one-off dynamic dates, through an external scheduler that fires exactly on that date and time.
A scheduled email tied to a booking can have its send date pushed automatically when the thing it's tied to changes — for example, a payment reminder moves if the payment deadline itself moves.

Every email attempt is logged with who it was sent to, what event triggered it, whether it succeeded, and the provider's response; staff can review these logs, export them, and resend any specific one.

Outside the templated-event system, staff (or an integrated chat tool) can send an ad-hoc email — for example, a chat transcript or a custom tour offer — using the same provider connection and logging.

rules.fact: An email only actually sends if its event is both active and marked available, has a configured provider template, and has a recipient address — otherwise the attempt is rejected and logged as failed with the specific reason.
A translated version of an event's content can only use the same dynamic-value placeholders already defined for that event; referencing an undefined placeholder is rejected.
Auto-translation never overwrites a translation a staff member already filled in by hand — it only fills in fields that are still empty.
Only one email provider connection can be active at a time; connecting a new one deactivates all others.

A scheduled email that has already been sent, or whose target record no longer applies (for example, a passenger-information update reminder for a booking that's since been cancelled), is skipped rather than sent.

permissions.fact: Managing email events, templates, recipients, translations, provider configuration, and viewing/resending logs from the admin all require an authenticated staff user, generally with standard staff model permissions.
Sending an ad-hoc chat email and running the scheduled-email dispatch job both run as the system itself via a machine API key, not as a staff action.

field_meanings.fact: "Is available" on an event controls whether it can be used to send mail at all; "is active" (standard on every record) is the usual on/off toggle — both must be true for an email to actually go out.

A dynamic value is a named placeholder (like a booking reference or a due date) an event's content can reference; only placeholders registered for that specific event are allowed in its content or translations.

An event-wise recipient sets a default to/cc/bcc address for a specific event — independent of whoever the email is actually about — for example, routing an internal notification to a fixed staff mailbox.

journeys.fact: A customer's booking milestone (confirmation, a payment reminder, a ticket update, and similar) automatically triggers the matching notification, rendered in their preferred language with their booking's real details, and sent through the tenant's connected provider — with a full log kept either way, so staff can find and resend anything that failed.

features.name: Surveys
features.summary: Customer surveys with dispatch and dispatch-status tracking.

workflows.fact: Surveys are created and managed in an external survey platform (Netigate) and synced into the tenant so staff can attach one to a tour.

The day before a tour with an attached survey returns, the platform automatically collects every traveling passenger on that tour's bookings who has an email address, and sends their details to the survey platform to create a personalized "sendout" — a batch of individually addressed survey links.

Passenger details sent to the survey platform include their name, gender, date of birth, phone number, and tour context (departure date/location, destination, tour guide, and skipper), so the survey provider can personalize or segment responses.
Once a sendout is created, each respondent's personal survey link is recorded, and a scheduled job emails that link to every respondent 24 hours after the sendout was scheduled.

rules.fact: Survey sendouts and their follow-up emails only run at all if the tenant's Netigate survey subscription add-on is active; otherwise both scheduled jobs report the subscription is inactive and do nothing.
Only passengers actually traveling on a booking, with a real email address, are included in a tour's survey sendout.
Each respondent only ever gets one survey email per sendout, even if they appear more than once in the respondent list.

permissions.fact: Viewing the synced list of surveys requires an authenticated staff user with standard model permissions; triggering a sync from the survey platform requires only an authenticated staff user.
Running a tour's survey sendout and sending its pending follow-up emails both run as the system itself via a machine API key on a schedule, not as a staff action.

field_meanings.fact: A survey dispatch's status is Pending (sendout created, follow-up email not yet sent), Sent (the follow-up email has gone out), or Failed.
"Activated" on a survey reflects whether it's turned on in the survey platform itself — kept in sync whenever surveys are synced.

journeys.fact: A passenger travels on a tour that has a survey attached; the day before the tour returns, they're added to that tour's survey sendout, and a day later they receive an email with their own personal link to fill it out.

side_effects.fact: The follow-up survey email is sent through the platform's own email notification system, using a dedicated feedback-email template.

features.name: Accounting Provider Setup & Reference Data
features.summary: Connecting an accounting provider (Fortnox/PowerOffice), syncing its projects/cost centers/VAT codes/customers, and mapping event accounts.

workflows.fact: Staff pick and connect one accounting provider (Fortnox or PowerOffice) by authorizing the connection with that provider; the platform stores the connection's access credentials and keeps them refreshed automatically.
Connecting a new provider automatically disconnects and deactivates any other provider that was previously configured — only one can be active for the tenant at a time.
Once connected, staff sync reference data from the accounting system into the platform: its projects, its cost centers, its VAT/tax codes, and its customer records.

Staff map each business event (like a new booking or a gift card sale) and scenario to the specific debit/credit accounts in the connected accounting system, optionally per currency, so postings land in the right place in the books.

rules.fact: Only one accounting provider connection can be active for a tenant at any time; activating one automatically deactivates all others.
Connection credentials are refreshed automatically on a schedule so the connection doesn't silently expire; each refresh has its own expiry window.

permissions.fact: Connecting, configuring, and syncing reference data for an accounting provider all require an authenticated staff user, generally with the standard staff model permissions; a few internal sync endpoints run as the system itself via a machine API key rather than as a staff action.

field_meanings.fact: A "project" and "cost center" are the accounting system's own way of tagging where revenue or cost belongs (for example, by department or initiative); this feature only mirrors them in so staff can assign postings to the right one.
A "scenario" groups the specific set of accounts a business event should post to — the same event (for example, a booking) can post differently depending on which scenario applies.

journeys.fact: Staff connect their accounting software once, sync its projects/cost centers/VAT codes into the platform, and map each business event's accounts — after that, the platform posts to the books automatically without staff repeating any of this setup per transaction.

features.name: Accounting Vouchers & Logs
features.summary: Automatic voucher posting on business events, request/response logging, and manual/batch resend.

workflows.fact: When a tracked business event happens (for example, a booking is created, a tour departs, a gift card is sold or redeemed, or an invoice is settled), the platform automatically builds an accounting voucher and sends it to the connected accounting provider.
Every attempt to post to the accounting provider is logged with the request sent and the response received, whether it succeeded, and which business event, booking, or transaction it relates to.
If posting a voucher failed (or needs to be re-sent for another reason), staff can resend that specific log, or resend every log matching a filter, from within the platform.
Whether a voucher successfully reached the accounting provider updates the related booking's or transaction's own accounting status, so staff can see at a glance whether it made it to the books.

rules.fact: A log that has already been successfully resent cannot be resent again — the system rejects a repeat attempt.
Logs for the automatic post-departure event (tour or yacht) can never be resent manually — those are only ever sent again by the platform's own automatic process, not by a staff click.
Bulk-resending logs by filter always skips the post-departure, invoice-payment, and settlement-invoice event types, since those are handled automatically rather than by manual resend.

permissions.fact: Viewing accounting logs and triggering a resend (single or batch) require an authenticated staff user; browsing the full internal log list additionally requires standard staff model permissions.

field_meanings.fact: A log's success flag reflects whether the connected accounting provider accepted the posting — not whether the underlying business event itself succeeded.

journeys.fact: A booking is created, departs, or gets paid; behind the scenes the platform posts the matching voucher to the connected accounting system and records the attempt as a log. If something goes wrong, staff can spot the failed log and resend it without redoing the underlying business action.

side_effects.fact: A successful or failed accounting post is reflected back onto the related booking or payment transaction as an accounting-sent status, which other features can read.

features.name: Supplier Invoices & Cost Registration
features.summary: Recording supplier invoices with cost/VAT account splits, registering actual supplier costs against bookings, and sending invoices to the connected accounting system.

workflows.fact: Staff record a supplier invoice — the amount owed, its VAT, due date, and which cost/VAT accounts it should be split across — and can attach it to the specific bookings it covers.

For each booking a supplier is involved in, staff (or the supplier's own system, via a company API token) register what that supplier actually charged for it, against what the platform had estimated it would cost — split by currency and by whether it was a room, an extra, or a flight itinerary.

Registering a supplier's actual cost against a booking marks the underlying cost line(s) on that booking as invoiced, so staff can see which costs still need a supplier invoice and which are already covered.

Staff can see a financial summary for an invoice (total, VAT, how much of it has been allocated to cost/VAT accounts and to specific bookings, and how much remains), and a status summary across all invoices (pending, paid, overdue totals).
If a supplier invoice is marked to be sent to the tenant's connected accounting system, the platform builds and sends it there automatically, and marks the invoice as sent once accepted.

rules.fact: A supplier invoice's due date defaults to its invoice date plus the supplier's own configured credit period, if no due date is given.

Registering the same supplier's cost against the same booking, currency, and invoice a second time adds to the previously registered amount rather than creating a separate record — unless that combination is explicitly not allowed to be updated, in which case it's rejected as a duplicate.
A supplier invoice's amount is automatically split into a cost-account entry and a VAT-account entry when it's created, so its totals always reconcile against those two accounts.

permissions.fact: Creating, viewing, and updating supplier invoices and registering costs against them from the admin all require an authenticated staff user with the standard staff model permissions.
A supplier's own system can be issued a separate company-level access token to list its own invoices and register its own costs against bookings, without needing a staff login.

field_meanings.fact: A supplier invoice's status is Pending, Paid, Unpaid, Canceled, or Sent To Accounting (once it's been posted to the tenant's connected accounting system).

"Estimate cost" is what the platform expected a supplier to charge for a booking (from its own room/extra/flight pricing); "invoice cost" is what the supplier actually invoiced for it — the difference is what staff reconcile.

journeys.fact: A booking uses a supplier for a room, an extra, or a flight; later, staff receive that supplier's invoice, record it with its cost/VAT split, and register how much of it applies to each affected booking — closing the loop between what was estimated and what was actually billed.

side_effects.fact: A supplier invoice sent to accounting posts through the same connected accounting provider used elsewhere in the platform.
